Fourth: Identifying the Identity of the Hostile Leadership and Cognitive Reframing of the Field (رابعاً: تحديد هوية القيادة المعادية وإعادة التأطير الإدراكي للميدان)

The prophetic logistical analysis was not limited to estimating the number, but extended to determining the "moral and leadership weight of the enemy." He asked the boys about the prominent leaders and nobles present in the army: "Who among the nobles of Quraish (قريش) is in it?"

They listed for him the names of the heads of disbelief and its leaders: Utbah bin Rabi'ah (عتبة بن ربيعة), Shaybah bin Rabi'ah (شيبة بن ربيعة), Abu Al-Bukhtari bin Hisham (أبو البختري بن هشام), Hakim bin Hizam (حكيم بن حزام), Nawfal bin Khuwaylid (نوفل بن خويلد), Al-Harith bin Amir (الحارث بن عامر), Tu'aymah bin Adiy (طعيمة بن عدي), Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith (النضر بن الحارث), Zam'ah bin Al-Aswad (زمعة بن الأسود), Abu Jahl bin Hisham (أبو جهل بن هشام), and Umayyah bin Khalaf (أمية بن خلف).

Faced with this list which included the fiercest champions and leaders of Mecca (مكة), the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not surrender to the logic of intimidation or discouragement; rather, he practiced the role of a wise leader in "cognitive reframing." He transformed this list, which was capable of instilling terror in the hearts of those with weak faith, into a massive tool for moral preparation for the army, turning to his Companions and saying with inspiring enthusiasm:

"This is Mecca (مكة); it has thrown to you the pieces of its liver!"

This psychological reframing shaped the fighting philosophy of the Companions according to the following dimensions:

  1. Transforming the Enemy from a Tyrannical Power into Approaching Spoils: Describing the leaders as "pieces of the liver" (which is the most precious and dearest thing owned by a person) stripped them of their "terrifying" character as an armed force with armor and swords, and added to them the quality of a "precious gift" presented by Mecca (مكة) to the Muslims.
  2. Creating Certainty in Breaking the Enemy’s Power: The presence of the first-row leaders in the field meant that their defeat in this battle would not be ordinary, but a fatal blow that would uproot the heads of polytheism and end Mecca's (مكة) pride forever, which was indeed achieved with the killing of most of this list in the battle.

These intelligence maneuvers and precise field analyses proved that the victory at Badr (بدر) was a carefully crafted outcome, in which truth of reliance and certainty combined with utmost vigilance and taking practical and scientific steps in reading traces, estimating forces, and managing information.

5. Media Propaganda and the Impact of Psychological Reframing on the Field (5. البروباجندا الإعلامية وأثر إعادة التأطير النفسي في الميدان)

Military battles are not managed by material weapons alone; psychological and media warfare represent a parallel weapon that may decide the battle before it begins. Controlling the morale of soldiers and shaping public awareness are the foundations for directing physical and field energies. The stage preceding the Battle of Badr (غزوة بدر الكبرى) witnessed an intense media and propaganda struggle between the two camps, presenting an important study in crowd psychology and the manufacture of public opinion. The "propaganda of shock and terror" led by Damdam bin Amr Al-Ghifari (ضمضم بن عمرو الغفاري) in Mecca (مكة) stood in contrast to the "genius of cognitive and psychological reframing" led by the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to direct the morale of his Companions in Medina (المدينة المنورة).

First: The Engineering of Panic by Damdam bin Amr: The Propaganda of Shock and Terror (أولاً: هندسة الهلع عند ضمضم بن عمرو: بروباجندا الصدمة والترعيب)

When Abu Sufyan (أبو سفيان) sensed the danger threatening the caravan, he did not send an ordinary messenger conveying the news coldly and quietly; rather, he hired Damdam bin Amr Al-Ghifari (ضمضم بن عمرو الغفاري), an expert in inciting public panic, and directed him to announce the call to arms in Mecca (مكة) using a dramatic style that captures minds and bypasses rational judgment to allow room only for the instinct of survival and defense of interests.

Damdam (ضمضم) used four symbolic and theatrical procedures in his entry into Mecca (مكة), designed to create a "visual and psychological shock" for the Meccan society:

  1. Mutilating his camel (cutting its nose and ears): Damdam (ضمضم) entered Mecca (مكة) while his camel was bleeding heavily from its face. "Cutting the nose of the camel" in the cultural traditions of the Arabs was the highest symbolic code indicating the occurrence of a devastating existential catastrophe and the approaching eradication of the tribe.
  2. Turning his saddle: He rode his camel backward or made its saddle inverted, as a clear visual signal that "matters have turned upside down," and that the balance of stability has been shattered.
  3. Tearing his shirt: He tore his clothes from the front and back, which is the traditional symbol expressing grief, tragedy, and approaching death, giving the observer the impression that they were looking at a man who barely escaped a horrific massacre.
  4. The panicked cry for the caravan: He stood in the valley bed at the Kaaba (الكعبة), screaming with all his strength, using the words most provocative to financial and security instincts:

    "O assembly of Quraish (قريش)! The caravan! The caravan! Your wealth with Abu Sufyan (أبو سفيان) has been intercepted by Muhammad (محمد) and his companions. I do not think you will reach it. Help! Help!"

This media methodology relies on "bypassing rational thought and inciting instinctive emotion" (Emotional Hijacking). When the Meccans saw a bleeding camel and a man with torn clothes screaming about the loss of their wealth (the caravan carrying their perfumes, trade, and foodstuffs on which the economy of Mecca [مكة] completely relied), their minds suspended thinking about causes or strategic calculations, and rushed directly toward a "panicked fight-or-flight response."

This shocking propaganda succeeded in transforming Mecca (مكة) within hours from a state of commercial relaxation to a state of comprehensive military mobilization. They all went out within a few days in an army of 1,300 fighters, driven by panic and fear for their pride and wealth.

Second: Critical Assessment of the Quraish Panic System (The Fragile Army) (ثانياً: التقييم النقدي لمنظومة الهلع القرشية (الجيش الهش))

Despite the rapid success of Damdam’s (ضمضم) propaganda in mobilizing fighters, military psychology confirms that "mobilization based on panic and momentary emotion produces an army that is fragile from a morale standpoint."

The army of Quraish (قريش) went out driven by:

  • The shock of fear of losing wealth.
  • The arrogant desire to display power (hypocrisy and pride).

Because the motive did not stem from a solid belief or a just cause, but rather from an "emotional reaction stirred by a panicked warner," this army carried the seeds of its defeat in its moral structure. As soon as the cause of panic disappeared (the safety of the caravan and Abu Sufyan [أبو سفيان]), the army began to break apart internally, and divisions appeared—such as the withdrawal of Bani Zuhrah (بني زهرة) and the reluctance of Bani Hashim (بني هاشم) to fight. An army mobilized by panic scatters as soon as the danger disappears or upon facing the first real field shock.

Third: The Genius of Prophetic Linguistic and Psychological Reframing: Turning Threat into Opportunity (ثالثاً: عبقرية التأطير اللغوي والنفسي النبوي: تحويل التهديد إلى فرصة)

In contrast, the Muslim community in Medina (المدينة المنورة) faced a completely different psychological and military challenge. They went out with simple weapons, without sufficient armor, and with only two horses, expecting to meet a caravan guarded by forty men, only to find themselves facing the army of Mecca (مكة) with all its fighting elite and champions (1,000 fighters, 100 horses, 600 coats of armor).

Here, the role of leadership in "cognitive reframing" emerged. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not deny the existence of the danger, nor did he resort to anesthesia or media lies; rather, he put his hand on the reality of the threat and re-formulated it linguistically and psychologically with his eloquent historic statement addressed to his Companions following the interrogation of the water-bearers:

"This is Mecca (مكة); it has thrown to you the pieces of its liver!"

This sentence is considered an early pioneering model in contemporary communication sciences for changing the context of perception (Reframing Context); it was based on two deep indications:

  1. The Metaphorical Indication ("Pieces of its liver"): In the Arabic tongue, "piece of the liver" is applied to the most precious and dearest thing owned by a person (such as a child or stored wealth). When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, applied this description to the leaders of the Quraish (قريش) army who went out to fight the Muslims, he stripped them of their "intimidating" character as a tyrannical force armed with armor and swords, and bestowed upon them the quality of a "precious gift" presented by Mecca (مكة) to the Muslims.
  2. Formulating an Opportunity Mindset Instead of a Threat Mindset: The threat represented by the presence of the fiercest leaders of Quraish (قريش) (Abu Jahl [أبو جهل], Utbah [عتبة], Shaybah [شيبة], Umayyah [أمية]) was transformed from a sign of "panic and fear of death" to a sign of a "golden strategic opportunity to eliminate the heads of disbelief with a single blow." The Companions understood from the phrase that Allah had led the elite of Mecca (مكة) to meet their end in this field, which would end Quraish's (قريش) pride and power forever, turning the natural human fear in their souls into advance and anticipation to fight and conquer the pieces of Mecca's (مكة) liver.

Fourth: Methodological Comparison Between Emotional Mobilization and Faith Commitment (رابعاً: المقارنة المنهجية بين التعبئة الانفعالية والالتزام الإيماني)

A comparative analysis of the two media and psychological methods reveals the fundamental differences between two schools in leading crowds:

Point of Comparison (وجه المقارنة) Quraish Propaganda (ضمضم بن عمرو) Prophetic Psychological Reframing (القيادة الإسلامية)
Tool of Mobilization Inciting panic, visual shock, terror, and prideful anger. Truthfulness, consultation, clarifying facts, and cognitive reframing.
Motives Stirred Protecting material interests (wealth) and preserving social standing and reputation (hypocrisy). Compliance with the command of Allah, realizing the creed, retrieving usurped rights, and seeking Paradise.
Nature of the Resulting Army Numerically and materially massive, but psychologically fragile, quickly dividing when the direct motivator disappears. Numerically and materially small, but psychologically solid, homogeneous, possessing the flexibility to transition from caravan to army with steadfastness.
Field Result Scattering of resolves, dispute at the signs of defeat, and rapid flight from the field (as Iblis and the polytheists did). Absolute steadfastness and patience in the face of the majority, and deserving victory and divine support.

The Battle of Badr (بدر) proved that psychological preparation based on truthfulness, reframing concepts, and linking hearts to Allah is the only guarantee for the cohesion of ranks and the manufacture of victory, while propaganda based on lies or panic remains a bubble that vanishes before the blows of truth.

6. The Psychology of the "Reluctant Army" and the Impact of Lack of Self-Motivation on Defeat (6. سيكولوجية "الجيش المكره" وأثر غياب الدافع الذاتي في الهزيمة)

Self-motivation and core conviction represent the primary driver of any human effort, and the importance of this psychological power multiplies in military fields, where human beings face the danger of death and annihilation. In contemporary military sciences, analysts agree that massive armies equipped with the latest weapons may collapse before a much smaller force if they suffer from a structural and psychological flaw represented by the "absence of a fighting doctrine" and the dominance of hatred for the obligation (the psychology of the reluctant army). The Quraish (قريش) camp in the Battle of Badr (بدر) presented a deeply analytical model of how the absence of self-conviction causes rapid military paralysis and ease of collapse and surrender to captivity before a solid, believing group.

First: The Structural Flaw in the Quraish Camp and the Collapse of the Justification for War (أولاً: الخلل الهيكلي في معسكر قريش وسقوط مبرر الحرب)

The army of Quraish (قريش) was established in its departure from Mecca (مكة) on a temporary, material motive: saving the commercial caravan and protecting the financial investments of the nobles of Mecca (مكة). Throughout their march toward the north, this motive was the only bond uniting the various clans of Quraish (قريش), who were living in a state of internal competition and conflict over sovereignty and leadership.

When Abu Sufyan (أبو سفيان) succeeded in maneuvering with the caravan and took the coastal route, achieving complete safety, he sent his famous message to the army:

"You only went out to protect your caravan, your men, and your wealth. Allah has saved them, so return."

Upon the arrival of this message, the "objective justification" for war collapsed in the minds of most fighters, as the material danger that brought them out had disappeared. Here, a major division emerged. Abu Jahl bin Hisham (أبو جهل بن هشام), with his pride and arrogance, insisted on continuing the march toward Badr (بدر) for the sake of show and pride:

"By Allah, we will not return until we reach Badr (بدر), stay there for three days... and the Arabs hear of our march, our gathering, and our power, so they will stand in awe of us forever."

This insistence by Abu Jahl (أبو جهل) transformed the nature of the battle in the minds of the soldiers from "defense of wealth and interests" to a "personal war of pride for Abu Jahl (أبو جهل)." Thus, the psychology of the "reluctant army" was formed, marched to the battlefield without real conviction in the utility of fighting or the justice of the cause.

Second: Al-Akhnas bin Shariq and Bani Zuhrah: The Withdrawal of the Pragmatic Mindset (ثانياً: الأخنس بن شريق وبنو زهرة: انسحاب العقلية البراجماتية)

The first manifestation of military paralysis resulting from the absence of motivation was shown in the stance of Al-Akhnas bin Shariq (الأخنس بن شريق), an ally of Bani Zuhrah (بني زهرة) and one of their wise leaders. Al-Akhnas (الأخنس) possessed a pragmatic (practical) mindset that weighed matters by actual profit and loss, away from Abu Jahl’s (أبو جهل) prideful arrogance.

Al-Akhnas (الأخنس) addressed Bani Zuhrah (بني زهرة) decisively, saying:

"O children of Zuhrah (زهرة)! Allah has saved your wealth and delivered your companion Abu Sufyan (أبو سفيان). You only went out to protect your wealth, so return, for there is no need for you to go out for something of no benefit..."

Bani Zuhrah (بني زهرة) obeyed Al-Akhnas (الأخنس) and they all returned to Mecca (مكة), not a single man staying behind. Approximately 300 fighters (representing about 23% of the total Meccan army) withdrew from the army.

  • This early withdrawal revealed the "fragility of the Quraish coalition"; the army was not a single unit united by a common creed, but a collection of interests that dissolved as soon as the individual benefit of each tribe was realized.
  • The withdrawal of Bani Zuhrah (بني زهرة) caused a severe morale shock to the rest of the army. They saw a quarter of their military strength withdraw out of conviction in the invalidity and futility of the war, which planted doubt in the hearts of those remaining and weakened their enthusiasm for fighting.

Third: Bani Hashim Under the Weight of Coercion: The Psychology of the Coerced Soldier (ثالثاً: بنو هاشم تحت وطأة الإكراه: سيكولوجية الجندي المجبر)

If Bani Zuhrah (بني زهرة) possessed the political and military capacity to withdraw because they were allies who owned their decision, other clans did not have this option and found themselves forced to fight a battle they did not believe in. At the head of these was Bani Hashim (بنو هاشم) (the tribe of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him).

Bani Hashim (بنو هاشم) represented the peak of the "coerced soldier" in the battlefield for the following reasons:

  1. Family and Kinship Ties: They went out to fight their sons and brothers—the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, Hamzah (حمزة), Ali (علي), and the emigrants from Bani Hashim (بني هاشم). Any killing in the battle would be a deep wound in the internal fabric of their tribe.
  2. Political Blackmail from Abu Jahl: Abu Jahl (أبو جهل) deliberately forced them to go out, questioning their loyalty to Quraish (قريش) and saying in a threatening tone: "By Allah, you shall not leave us until we return." They went out while harboring hatred for the war and detesting the tyrannical leadership of Abu Jahl (أبو جهل).

The coerced soldier completely lacks the "offensive drive" in fighting; he enters the battlefield with his sole concern being "survival and escaping with the least losses." During the fighting, these soldiers turn into a genuine burden on their leadership; they do not show resilience in difficult situations, and they surrender to captivity willingly at the first sign of breaking ranks, and may even turn against their leadership morally during the course of the battle.

Fourth: Field Impact: Voluntary Submission and Ease of Capture (رابعاً: الأثر الميداني: الاستسلام الطوعي وسهولة الأسر)

This defeated psychology of the "reluctant army" translated practically during the course of the battle into a striking phenomenon: the ease of capturing Quraish’s (قريش) champions and reluctant men, and their rapid surrender without real fighting.

This field impact was embodied in two prominent models:

  • Al-Abbas (العباس): He was a massive man, a horseman, possessing immense physical strength. Nevertheless, he was captured in the battle by a short, physically weak Ansari companion, Kab bin Amr (كعب بن عمرو) [Abu Al-Yasar (أبو اليسر)], may Allah be pleased with him.

    When analyzing this incident psychologically and militarily, we find that Al-Abbas (العباس), may Allah be pleased with him, surrendered willingly and did not show any significant resistance to his weak captor; because he was guided by a "reluctance to confront and fight" and an internal desire not to spill a drop of Muslim blood, so captivity was a safe exit for him from the dilemma of fighting which he was forced into. When the Companions wondered how Abu Al-Yasar (أبو اليسر) captured him despite that physical disparity, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, explained the unseen support aiding physical certainty to reassure souls.

  • Abu Al-As bin Al-Rabi' (أبو العاص بن الربيع): He was also captured with extreme ease. He did not carry any ideological grudge against the Muslims, and he loved his wife and his father-in-law, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. He went out under the weight of Meccan social and tribal pressure, so his captivity was voluntary in reality due to the absence of a fighting motive.

Fifth: Smart Prophetic Guidance and Deciphering the Code of the "Reluctant Army" (خامساً: التوجيه النبوي الذكي وتفكيك شفرة "الجيش المكره")

The military intelligence and psychological depth of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was evident in his precise knowledge of the spiritual and psychological compositions of the enemy's camp. He issued a strict military command to his soldiers before the start of the battle, reflecting his full understanding of the phenomenon of "coerced soldiers":

"I have known that men from Bani Hashim (بني هاشم) and others have been brought out by force, having no need to fight us. So whoever of you meets anyone from Bani Hashim (بني هاشم), let him not kill him; and whoever meets Abu Al-Bukhtari bin Hisham (أبو البختري بن هشام), let him not kill him; and whoever meets Al-Abbas bin Abd Al-Muttalib (العباس بن عبد المطلب), let him not kill him, for he was brought out by force." (Narrated by Ibn Hisham [ابن هشام] and Abu Dawud [أبو داود]).

This smart military command achieved immense strategic and psychological benefits:

  1. Dismantling the Enemy's Cohesion Psychologically: When the coerced soldiers in the Quraish (قريش) army learned that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had ordered their blood to be spared and to avoid killing them, their desire to surrender increased, and any remaining incentive they had to resist and fight collapsed, hastening the collapse of the Quraish (قريش) rank.
  2. Preserving Future Social Relations: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saw with the eye of insight and mercy that these coerced individuals would be the leaders and soldiers of Islam in the future (as happened with Al-Abbas [العباس] and Abu Al-As [أبو العاص] later). Preserving their lives was a strategic gain for the emerging state.

Sixth: Geopolitical and Qur'anic Assessment of the Phenomenon of "Diverse Hearts" (سادساً: التقييم الجيوسياسي والقرآني لظاهرة "شتات القلوب")

The Qur'an summarizes the fragile structural nature of the forces of falsehood that lack a creed and a common motive, which appear outwardly cohesive and massive, but are in reality collapsed and empty:

{لَا يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ جَمِيعًا إِلَّا فِي قُرًى مُّحَصَّنَةٍ أَوْ مِن وَرَاءِ جُدُرٍ ۚ بَأْسُهُم بَيْنَهُم شَدِيدٌ ۚ تَحْسَبُهُمْ جَمِيعًا وَقُلُوبُهُمْ شَتَّىٰ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَّا يَعْقِلُونَ}
"They will not fight you all except within fortified cities or from behind walls. Their adversary among themselves is severe. You think they are together, but their hearts are diverse. That is because they are a people who do not reason." [Surah Al-Hashr: 14] (الحشر: 14).

The miraculous divine phrase {تَحْسَبُهُمْ جَمِيعًا وَقُلُوبُهُمْ شَتَّىٰ} (You think they are together, but their hearts are diverse) is the precise description of the Quraish (قريش) army at Badr (بدر); their bodies were gathered under one banner, and their horses and armor dazzled observers and suggested cohesion and power, but their hearts were diverse. Among them were those who fought for hypocrisy and pride (Abu Jahl [أبو جهل]), those who fought coerced and fearing for themselves and their kinship (Bani Hashim [بنو هاشم]), and those who lay in wait for others.

In contrast, the Muslim army represented a single body whose soldiers' hearts melted into one creed and absolute self-conviction. Thus, truthfulness and ethical clarity triumphed over the fragile majority and diverse hearts, deciding forever that victory is a spiritual and creedal creation that begins in the depths of souls and convictions before starting in the fields of weapons and equipment.

1. Linguistic Double Entendre as an Intelligence Tool: The "We are from Water" Tactic (1. التورية اللغوية كأداة استخباراتية: تكتيك "نحن من ماء")

First: Moral Honesty and Information Security in Islam (أولاً: الصدق الأخلاقي والأمن المعلوماتي في الإسلام)

The military doctrine in Islam is built upon a unique and delicate balance between strict moral commitment and the security vigilance and tactical maneuvering required by the circumstances of war. Honesty in the Islamic conception is not merely a social value, but an authentic pillar of faith and the building of the Muslim personality; as Allah the Almighty said in His clear revelation:

{يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَكُونُوا مَعَ الصَّادِقِينَ}
"O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with those who are true." [Surah At-Tawbah: 119] (التوبة: 119).

Despite this decisive emphasis on honesty, Islamic jurisprudence, with its flexibility and realism, considered the nature of military conflicts, which cannot succeed in the field without concealing plans, prohibiting information leaks, and obscuring the enemy. The established Prophetic rule in this field is what is proven in the Sahihayn (Al-Bukhari and Muslim) from his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: «War is deception» ("الحَرْبُ خُدْعَةٌ").

From here emerged the jurisprudence of "indirect speech and double entendre" (المعاريض والتورية) as a legitimate and practical solution that combines preserving the sanctity of absolute honesty while achieving the utmost security necessity in war. It is narrated from the Companions and Successors that they said: «Indeed, in indirect speech (المعاريض) there is enough to dispense with lying.»

Indirect speech or double entendre (التورية) is when a speaker utters a word that bears two meanings: one close, which comes to the listener's mind but is not intended, and the other distant, which is the true meaning intended by the speaker, and both meanings are correct in origin. The genius of this linguistic tactic is manifested in its most brilliant form during the intelligence reconnaissance phase that preceded the clash of the two armies in the Great Battle of Badr (بدر).

Second: Reconnaissance of the Field and the Encounter with Sufyan al-Damri (ثانياً: الاستطلاع الميداني واللقاء مع سفيان الضمري)

After the Muslims traveled from the area of Dhufran (ذفران) and took the rugged mountain passes towards Badr (بدر), they camped near the wells. In those critical moments, the flow of information represented the difference between victory and defeat; the enemy was near, the forces were unequal, and secrecy was the first line of defense.

The military leadership did not rely only on transmitted reports, but the leader himself, Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, went out with his companion Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (أبو بكر الصديق), may Allah be pleased with him, on an advanced reconnaissance tour to stand on the geography of the land and the movements of the enemy; which in itself represents a leadership style that relies on direct field inspection.

While roaming the desert, they came across an Arab sheikh living in those areas, Sufyan al-Damri (سفيان الضمري). Here began the process of smart intelligence negotiation; as the Prophet wanted to obtain information without revealing his military or political identity lest the news leak to Quraysh. He asked him about Quraysh, about Muhammad (محمد) and his companions, and what news he had heard from both sides.

The Arab sheikh showed Bedouin intelligence and caution; as he realized that the questioners were not ordinary passersby, he refused to provide information for free and said: "I will not inform you until you inform me of who you are?"

Here, the Muslims did not resort to threatening with force or using violence to extract information, but rather the smart diplomacy of information barter was used. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him: «If you inform us, we will inform you.»

The sheikh asked for reassurance: "Is that for that?" (meaning, is this a fair exchange of news for news?), he replied: «Yes.»

When the sheikh was reassured by the agreement, he provided intelligence information of extreme precision in geographical and temporal specification, saying: "I have been informed that Muhammad (محمد) and his companions set out on such and such a day, and if the one who informed me told the truth, they are today in such and such a place (which is the exact actual location of the Muslims' camp); and I have been informed that Quraysh set out on such and such a day, and if the one who informed me told the truth, they are today in such and such a place (which is the exact actual location of the Quraysh army)."

By virtue of this report, the leadership obtained an additional double confirmation of geographical data: it determined its actual location relative to the enemy, and accurately identified the coordinates of the enemy camp.

Third: The Tactic of Linguistic Double Entendre: "We are from Water" (ثالثاً: تكتيك التورية اللغوية: "نحن من ماء")

As soon as the sheikh finished his talk and fulfilled his commitment, he immediately demanded his dues from the information deal and asked: "Who are you from?"

The direct answer (We are Muhammad and Abu Bakr from Medina) would have meant the collapse of the entire security system of the expedition; as the sheikh is a Bedouin who might talk to the riders, or this information might fall into the hands of the spies of Abu Sufyan (أبو سفيان) or Quraysh. At the same time, explicit lying contradicts the infallibility and noble Prophetic morals.

Here came the genius, eloquent answer that resolved the situation with the fewest words: «We are from water» ("نَحْنُ مِنْ مَاءٍ").

They quickly departed from him immediately after throwing this sentence to cut off any other investigative tactical questions that might spoil the security purpose of the obscuration.

The sheikh Sufyan al-Damri (سفيان الضمري) stood stunned, turning the word in his mind and trying to decode its linguistic and geographical puzzle based on the data of his environment, and began to wonder in astonishment: "What 'from water'? From the water of Iraq (العراق)?"

The sheikh's mind immediately turned to the "close meaning" that comes to the minds of Arabs in the desert; which is that the two riders belong to a tribe residing near a famous water source, or that they are coming from the direction of the rivers of Iraq (Tigris and Euphrates), which are called "the water of Iraq". This mental diversion completely scattered the sheikh's focus, making him completely rule out that these two men are the vanguard of the nearby army of Medina; which secured the movement of the Muslims and preserved the secrecy of their locations.

Fourth: Jurisprudential and Rhetorical Foundation of the Prophetic Double Entendre (رابعاً: التأصيل الفقهي والبلاغي للتورية النبوية)

The tactic of «We are from water» ("نَحْنُ مِنْ مَاءٍ") represents the pinnacle of rhetorical employment in the service of military and security politics. Analyzing this situation requires standing on its legitimate and linguistic dimensions through the following facts:

The distant and true intended meaning of the Prophetic phrase was to refer to the primary material from which man and all humanity were created; and this meaning is confirmed by definitive texts from the Holy Quran that decided this scientific and legitimate fact centuries before its discovery:

  • The origin of the creation of life: Allah the Almighty said: {وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ ۖ أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ} ("And We made from water every living thing; then will they not believe?") [Surah Al-Anbiya: 30] (الأنبياء: 30).
  • The origin of the creation of humans: Allah the Almighty said: {وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ الْمَاءِ بَشَرًا فَجَعَلَهُ نَسَبًا وَصِهْرًا ۗ وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيرًا} ("And it is He who created from water a human being and made him [a relative by] lineage and marriage. And ever is your Lord competent.") [Surah Al-Furqan: 54] (الفرقان: 54).
  • The nature of the human material: Allah the Almighty said: {أَلَمْ نَخْلُقكُّم مِّن مَّاءٍ مَّهِينٍ} ("Did We not create you from a liquid of little value?") [Surah Al-Mursalat: 20] (المرسلات: 20). And He, the Majestic and Exalted, said: {فَلْيَنظُرِ الْإِنسَانُ مِمَّ خُلِقَ * خُلِقَ مِن مَّاءٍ دَافِقٍ} ("Let man observe from what he was created. He was created from a fluid, ejected.") [Surah At-Tariq: 5-6] (الطارق: 5-6).

Based on this Quranic foundation, the phrase «We are from water» ("نَحْنُ مِنْ مَاءٍ") is pure truth and a scientific and existential fact in which there is no lie or evasion before Allah the Almighty; for all humans are from water. Thus, the double entendre (التورية) succeeded in protecting the military purpose without tarnishing honest morals.

This incident establishes a firm jurisprudential rule in the jurisprudence of calling to Allah, struggle, and international relations; which is that the use of symbols, indirect speech, and double entendre is legitimate and required when there is need and necessity. In the context of wars, supreme interests emerge related to the preservation of souls and lives, and the protection of the core of religion and state. And because explicit lying demolishes the wall of moral trust, double entendre (التورية) represents the "safe exit" (المندوحة) that achieves the military goal and preserves the dignity of the tongue, keeping it safe from blameworthy lying and fabrication.

Fifth: Security and Strategic Dimensions of the "From Water" Tactic (خامساً: الأبعاد الأمنية والاستراتيجية لتكتيك "نحن من ماء")

When deconstructing this event from the perspective of contemporary security and military sciences, we find that it involves extremely important strategic dimensions:

  • Preventive Security and Prohibition of Information Leakage: In the open desert environment, undisciplined mouths represent the largest security loophole that overthrows strategic secrecy. If the sheikh had known the identity of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his companion, he might have spoken of it inadvertently in front of any Quraysh reconnaissance detachment or spies belonging to Abu Sufyan (أبو سفيان). Therefore, obscuration here was a proactive preventive step to protect the back of the Islamic army.
  • Positive Deception and Manufacturing Mental Confusion: The Prophetic tactic did not suffice with obscuration, but rather led the listener's mind to "temporary positive deception"; where the sheikh's mind was preoccupied with searching for the geography of Iraq (العراق) and its distant waters from the hot geography of the Hijaz. This mental diversion secured for the Muslims additional precious time to move and maneuver before Quraysh realized their actual approach to the wells of Badr (بدر).
  • Direct Exploratory Leadership and Control of Information Sources: The emergence of the supreme leadership itself to collect information confirms that intelligence activity in the jurisprudence of battles is not a secondary work left to amateurs or relied upon by chance; rather, it is a fundamental pillar practiced by the leader himself to ensure the accuracy and correctness of data and to build fateful decisions upon it.

The tactic of «We are from water» ("نَحْنُ مِنْ مَاءٍ") remains a historical witness that rhetoric, eloquence, and the strength of linguistic argument can become in times of crises and wars more effective and sharper than the edge of swords and the positions of spears.

2. Jurisprudence of Distinguishing Between Legislative Revelation and Military Opinion: The Methodology of Al-Hubab bin al-Mundhir (2. فقه التمييز بين الوحي التشريعي والرأي العسكري: منهجية الحباب بن المنذر)

First: Cognitive Foundations for Distinguishing Ranks of Prophetic Speech (أولاً: الأسس المعرفية لتمييز رتب الكلام النبوي)

Accurate understanding of the nature of Prophetic dispositions and their methodological classification represents one of the most important cognitive foundations in Islamic thought and principles of jurisprudence. The noble Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, thanks to their companionship with the revelation and the owner of the message, Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, formed a deep methodological consciousness that distinguishes between the ranks of Prophetic speech and dispositions. They realized that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had two main stations in his address and guidance:

The First Station: The Station of Message, Conveyance, and Legislation (مقام الرسالة والتبليغ والتشريع): This is the infallible station in which he receives revelation from Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, and conveys it to the Ummah as creed, Sharia, and rulings of halal and haram. In this station, there is no room for human reasoning or intellectual opposition, but rather it is the place of complete submission and absolute compliance. The Holy Quran has regulated this station with decisive rules:

  • Prohibition of choice before His decree: Allah the Almighty said: {وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلَا مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ...} ("It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should [thereafter] have any choice about their affair...") [Surah Al-Ahzab: 36] (الأحزاب: 36).
  • The intertwining of faith with absolute submission: Allah the Almighty said: {فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّىٰ يُقَوِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُوا فِي أَنفُسِهِمْ حَرَجًا مِّمَّا قَضَيْتَ وَيُسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا} ("But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in [full, willing] submission.") [Surah An-Nisa: 65] (النساء: 65).
  • Linking obedience to the Messenger with obedience to Allah: Allah the Almighty said: {مَّن يُطِعِ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدْ أَطَاعَ اللَّهَ...} ("He who obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah...") [Surah An-Nisa: 80] (النساء: 80).

The Second Station: The Station of Humanity, Worldly Experience, and Field Management (مقام البشرية والخبرة الدنيوية والتدبير الميداني): This is the station in which the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, acted according to human nature, life experience, and military and political estimation (opinion, war, stratagem, pollination of palm trees, and trade). In this station, the door was opened wide for the human mind for reasoning, consultation, discussion, and correction, based on material laws and human experiences. The Prophetic Sunnah has established this methodological distinction in various situations, including what Imam Muslim narrated in his Sahih in the story of pollinating palm trees, where the Prophet said: «You know best about the affairs of your world.»

Second: The Methodology of Al-Hubab bin al-Mundhir in Badr (ثانياً: منهجية الحباب بن المنذر في بدر)

This methodological approach was manifested in its highest applied forms during the descent of the Islamic army in the valley of Badr (بدر). When the Muslims moved towards the wells of Badr to cut off the road to the army of the polytheists, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, camped with the army at the nearest well to the wells of Badr (i.e., the first well encountered by someone coming from Medina).

The Companion, expert in military affairs and the natural geography of the area, Al-Hubab bin al-Mundhir bin al-Jamuh (الحباب بن المنذر بن الجموح), may Allah be pleased with him, saw that this position involved a tactical flaw; as camping the army at the first well left the rest of the wells behind open to the army of the polytheists, enabling them to drink and secure water logistics, while the Muslims might fall into a thirst crisis if the fighting was prolonged.

But Al-Hubab, out of proper upbringing, etiquette, and methodology, did not present his military opinion directly as an opposition to the leader's decision, but rather he presented before his consultation a great methodological question that is the key to legislative consciousness: "O Messenger of Allah, is this camp a camp that Allah descended you to, so we cannot advance or retreat from it, or is it opinion, war, and stratagem?"

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, answered him with clarity, scientific honesty, and leadership humility: «Rather, it is opinion, war, and stratagem.»

Here, after Al-Hubab made sure that the position was not a direction from infallible revelation, but rather a field of mental choice and field management subject to the laws of war, he gave his technical tactical opinion with all confidence and scientific courage, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, this is not a camp. Set out with the people until we come to the nearest water to the people (i.e., the well closest to the army of Mecca), then we camp there, then we ruin (block and bury) what is behind it of the wells, then we build a basin over it and fill it with water, then we fight the people, so we drink and they do not drink."

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, listened to the consultation with an open mind and appreciation for the people of specialization, and he did not find any discomfort in himself to retract from his first decision in favor of the most correct opinion; so he said encouragingly: «You have advised with opinion.»

And he rose with the army immediately and implemented the plan proposed by Al-Hubab bin al-Mundhir.

Third: Methodological and Fundamental Analysis of Al-Hubab's Position (ثالثاً: التحليل المنهجي والأصولي لموقف الحباب بن المنذر)

This historical position involves extremely important methodological and fundamental benefits that draw the boundaries between religious text and the human mind:

  • Al-Hubab bin al-Mundhir expressed through his saying: "Is it a camp that Allah descended you to..." the creed of absolute submission to the established legitimate text. If it becomes clear to the Muslim that the matter is directed from the niche of revelation (an explicit definitive text in proof and indication), then the role of the mind here is summarized in understanding, compliance, and exerting effort in application, not in trying to dispute the text or searching for justifications to circumvent it under the pretext of imagined interest; for the true interest lies in following the infallible revelation.
  • When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, approved that the position was subject to "opinion, war, and stratagem", he freed the Muslim mind from the burden of waiting for revelation in the details of material sciences and worldly tactics; for the Sharia did not come to abolish the minds of humans in the fields of their experimental specialization (such as medicine, engineering, architecture, military sciences, and management), but rather urged the employment of the mind and exhausting the effort in these fields according to the running cosmic traditions.

Certainly, this methodological distinction protects Islamic thought from two dangerous deviations:

  1. The First Deviation (Politicizing or Generalizing Sanctity): Which is imposing a character of sanctity and legitimate obligation on human opinions and reasoning that are subject to error and correctness in the fields of politics, management, and war, which leads to paralysis of thinking and closing the door to human development.
  2. The Second Deviation (Interpreting or Diluting Constants): Which is subjecting the fixed worship and legislative legitimate texts to the fluctuations of minds and desires under the pretext of modernization and development, which empties the Sharia of its sanctity and spiritual and moral stability.

Fourth: Evidence from the Biography of Consolidating This Methodology (رابعاً: شواهد من السيرة على ترسيخ هذه المنهجية)

The position of Al-Hubab in Badr was not a fleeting event, but rather part of a consistent Prophetic methodology to educate the Companions to employ their minds in the fields of opinion and management. Among the confirmed evidence of that:

  • The consultation of Salman al-Farisi (سلمان الفارسي) in Al-Khandaq (Battle of the Trench): When the crowds of the Parties overwhelmed Medina, the Companions did not wait for a revelation to descend with the details of fortification; rather Salman stepped forward, based on his war experience in the land of Persia, and proposed digging the trench as a defensive strategy that the Arabs were not familiar with, so the Prophet accepted it and implemented it immediately.
  • The consultation of the two Sa'ds in the reconciliation of Ghatafan: During the siege of the Parties, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, wanted to relieve the military pressure by reconciling the tribe of Ghatafan on a third of the fruits of Medina so they would withdraw. Before concluding the agreement, he consulted Sa'd bin Mu'adh (سعد بن معاذ) and Sa'd bin Ubadah (سعد بن عبادة), may Allah be pleased with them, so they asked with a methodological question similar to the question of Al-Hubab: "O Messenger of Allah, is it a matter that you love so we do it, or something that Allah commanded you with that we must do, or something you do for us?" He said: «Rather, something I do for you.» They said with strength and pride based on estimating the situation in the field: "By Allah, we will not give them except the sword." The Prophet smiled and acceded to their opinion and retracted from the reconciliation of Ghatafan.

Fifth: Reflection of the Methodology on the Contemporary Reality of the Ummah (خامساً: انعكاس المنهجية على الواقع المعاصر للأمة)

The Islamic Ummah today is in dire need of restoring the methodology of Al-Hubab bin al-Mundhir to reformulate its civilizational and intellectual reality:

  • Respecting Scientific and Field Specialization: Just as the Prophet (who was supported by revelation) retreated before the military specialization of Al-Hubab, decision-makers and leaders must listen to the people of specialization and experience in every field (economy, medicine, politics, and technology), and entrust matters to their qualified people.
  • Combining Revelation and Experimental Mind: Civilizational rise requires adhering to the sanctity of revelation in its great values, moral constants, and legislation (the capital of identity and spirit), with the utmost openness and flexibility in importing and developing modern material sciences, mechanisms, and systems (the capital of strength and empowerment). While we unite our spiritual Qibla towards the Kaaba in submission to revelation, we direct our minds to study cosmic traditions and earthly tactics in victory for "opinion, war, and stratagem".

3. Flexibility of Prophetic Leadership and Creating Intellectual Safety Space for Soldiers (3. مرونة القيادة النبوية وتخليق مساحات الأمان النفسي والفكري للجنود)

First: The Concept of Psychological and Intellectual Safety in Leadership (أولاً: مفهوم الأمان النفسي والفكري في القيادة)

Modern military and administrative leadership theories agree that the success of any system depends primarily on its cultural and educational climate; for material and numerical capability is of no value if the environment is repelling to competencies or disabling to minds. In this context, the concept of "Psychological and Intellectual Safety" (الأمان النفسي والفكري) emerged as one of the most important conditions for organizational and field effectiveness; and it means: "The general climate in which the individual feels completely safe to tell the truth, express opinion, criticize prevailing ideas, and propose alternative solutions, without fear of punishment, marginalization, ridicule, or accusation in loyalty."

The absence of this safety produces the phenomenon of "Organizational Silence" (الصمت التنظيمي), where the soldier or member sees the flaw with certainty, but prefers silence and compliance out of fear of the leadership's tyranny or the group's blame, which leads entities to certain disasters. In contrast, manufacturing this safety releases "collective intelligence", stimulates initiative, and makes every individual feel that they are a partner in responsibility and not just a machine to implement blind orders.

The Prophetic leadership established this concept and deepened it in the souls of the Ummah since the first moments of establishing the state; for consultation and flexibility were not just formal procedures, but rather a complete "educational philosophy" concerned with building the free human capable of thinking, initiative, and review with all etiquette and pride.

Second: The Educational Structure of "Intellectual Safety" in the Muslims' Camp (ثانياً: البنية التربوية لـ "الأمان الفكري" في معسكر المسلمين)

The question of Al-Hubab bin al-Mundhir in Badr: "Is it a camp that Allah descended you to... or is it opinion, war, and stratagem?" was not to be issued by a soldier unless he was relying on a thick wall of psychological safety built by the great leader, Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, over thirteen years in Mecca and two years in Medina. The Companions realized that their minds were respected, their opinions appreciated, and the leadership did not narrow criticism or guidance in the places of human reasoning.

The features of this Prophetic safety are manifested through the following legitimate foundations: The Holy Quran laid the foundations of flexible and merciful leadership that brings hearts closer and opens minds, warning against authoritarian, harsh leadership that repels followers and disperses the gathering; as Allah the Almighty said in the divine direction to the Messenger, Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him:

{فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ اللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمْ ۖ وَلَوْ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ الْقَلْبِ لَانفَضُّوا مِنْ حَوْلِكَ ۖ فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ...}
"So by mercy from Allah, [O Muhammad], you were gentle with them. And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from about you. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter..." [Surah Ali 'Imran: 159] (آل عمران: 159).

This verse decides a unique leadership constitution; for the Prophet—who was supported by revelation and guided from heaven—was commanded with gentleness, forgiveness, and seeking forgiveness for followers, and consulting them in the finest details of public and military affairs. The purpose of consultation here is not only to bring the most correct opinion, but rather it is primarily "manufacturing the Ummah" and preparing it to bear responsibilities and train to make decisions, for the Ummah to learn that its opinion is a partner in manufacturing victory and empowerment.

The first generation was raised to believe that expressing opinion and proposing amendments to plans is part of the advice obligatory for religion and leadership, and not a departure from obedience or a doubt in competence; in the authentic hadith narrated by Imam Muslim: «Religion is advice», it was said: To whom, O Messenger of Allah? He said: «To Allah, His Book, His Messenger, and the leaders of the Muslims and their commonality.»

Therefore, we saw the eyes of the Emigrants and Helpers reviewing the leadership with all courage and etiquette in Badr, Uhud (أُحُد), Al-Khandaq (الخندق), and Al-Hudaybiyyah (الحديبية); because they were fully convinced that their minds were partners in formulating the field reality, and the Prophetic leadership appreciated "feedback" from the people of specialization and experience.

Third: The Psychology of Oppression and Dictatorship in the Camp of Quraysh (ثالثاً: سيكولوجية الاستبداد والقهر في معسكر قريش: أبو جهل نموذجاً)

In complete contrast to the camp of Muslims based on tranquility and intellectual safety, the camp of Quraysh was suffering under the weight of the "psychology of oppression and arrogance" led by Abu Jahl bin Hisham (أبو جهل بن هشام). The events preceding the Battle of Badr presented a live model of how authoritarian leadership causes silencing wise minds, paralyzing strategic thinking, and driving the army to its doom against its will.

This catastrophic scene was manifested through the following situations: When the survival of the caravan and Abu Sufyan was confirmed, Utbah bin Rabi'ah (عتبة بن ربيعة)—who was one of the great masters and sages of Quraysh—stood addressing the people, advising them to return, spare blood, avoid fighting relatives, offering to pay the blood money of Amr bin al-Hadrami (عمرو بن الحضرمي) from his own money to cut off the pretext of revenge.

When Abu Jahl bin Hisham heard this rational initiative that almost gathered Quraysh on peace and return, he did not discuss it with the scale of mind or strategic interest, but rather immediately resorted to using the usual weapons of authoritarian leadership:

  • Stabbing honor, courage, and accusing of treason: He accused Utbah of cowardice, fleeing from the march, and fear for his son Abu Hudhayfah bin Utbah (أبو حذيفة بن عتبة) who was a Muslim in the camp of Medina, using the offensive, insulting phrase in Arab customs: "By Allah, his spleen (his lung from fear) swelled when he saw Muhammad and his companions!"
  • Emotional blackmail and stirring instinctive revenge rancor: He immediately sent to Amir bin al-Hadrami (عامر بن الحضرمي) (the brother of the killed) to stir his zeal, and said to him: "This is your ally (Utbah) who wants to return with the people, and you have seen your revenge with your own eyes, so get up and chant your protection and the killing of your brother." So Amir stood up screaming and shouting, uncovering his shame to the idols of ignorance: "Woe to Amr! Woe to Amr!" The people were inflamed, the cauldron boiled with blood, and the wise advice of Utbah bin Rabi'ah was invalidated.

This intellectual and social terrorism practiced by Abu Jahl bin Hisham caused the paralysis of the will of Utbah bin Rabi'ah; for despite his certain knowledge that proceeding in this battle was suicide and a destructive strategic error, and despite his severe anger at Abu Jahl's offense and his threat to him, saying: "The one who makes his anus small will know whose spleen swelled, me or him?", he did not possess the moral courage to stick to his position; so he surrendered to the pressure of the group and led his people to fighting and doom out of pre-Islamic fanaticism and refusal of the stigma of cowardice, so he was the first to be killed in the individual duel in Badr.

This Pharaonic model is the actual embodiment of the Quranic warning of the fate of blind obedience to the corrupt authoritarian leadership:

  • The fate of the followers of Pharaoh (فرعون): Allah the Almighty said: {فَاتَّبَعُوا أَمْرَ فِرْعَوْنَ ۖ وَمَا أَمْرُ فِرْعَوْنَ بِرَشِيدٍ * يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ النَّارَ...} ("So they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not [one of] right. He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire...") [Surah Hud: 97-98] (هود: 97-98).
  • The philosophy of Pharaonic autocracy: Allah the Almighty said on the tongue of Pharaoh: {مَا أُرِيكُمْ إِلَّا مَا أَرَىٰ وَمَا أَهْدِيكُمْ إِلَّا سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ} ("I do not show you except what I see, and I do not guide you except to the path of right conduct.") [Surah Ghafir: 29] (غافر: 29).

Abu Jahl bin Hisham was truly the "Pharaoh of this Ummah", and he applied the same Pharaonic oppressive methodology that leads its followers, overriding their opinion, to the resources of destruction and perishing.

Fourth: Behavioral and Field Comparison Between the Two Camps (رابعاً: المقارنة السلوكية والميدانية بين المعسكرين)

The psychological and behavioral analysis of the battlefield reveals vast fundamental differences between the effects of intellectual safety and the effects of authoritarian oppression on the morale and performance of fighters:

Aspect of Comparison (وجه المقارنة) Camp of Muslims (Prophetic Leadership) Camp of Polytheists (Ignorant Leadership)
Psychological Climate Absolute safety; confidence in self, freedom of expression, review, and initiative. Intellectual terrorism and oppression; dominance of fear of accusation of cowardice or treason.
Value of Mind and Specialization Advanced and respected; leadership accedes to the consultation of the expert without arrogance. Wasted and excluded; the minds of great masters (like Utbah) are trivialized and canceled for the arrogance of Abu Jahl.
Spirit of Initiative for Soldiers Very high; every individual feels his personal responsibility for protecting the rank. Non-existent; the army is driven reluctantly against its will and strategic convictions.
Cohesion During Crisis Extreme solidity; a rank aligned like a structure, each part strengthening the other. Disintegration and division; different hearts and hidden dispute that explodes at the first field shock.

Fifth: Contemporary Educational and Practical Dimensions (خامساً: الأبعاد التربوية والعملية المعاصرة)

The educational structure built by the Prophetic leadership confirms that achieving "psychological and intellectual safety" is not an intellectual luxury or a secondary administrative option, but rather a legitimate duty and an urgent strategic requirement for building rational entities:

  • Breaking the idol of autocracy and the single opinion: If the infallible, Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, consulted and acceded to the opinion of his soldiers to soothe their hearts and educate their minds, how is it permissible for those below him of leaders, rulers, scholars, and educators to autocratize their opinions and refuse review and advice?
  • Encouraging a culture of initiative and constructive criticism: Institutions and educational, social, and administrative systems in the Ummah must formulate a safe environment that welcomes questions, opens spaces for meaningful discussion, respects the minds of the generation, and rewards innovators and owners of initiatives; for from here are born the exceptional competencies that lead change.
  • The difference between the pride of advice and the foolishness of transgression: The Prophetic biography taught us that intellectual safety is based on pride and etiquette together; for the Companions reviewed with all courage and strength, but they did not transgress or trivialize the leadership, rather they knew that mutual respect is the moral cover that protects the spaces of intellectual safety from chaos and dilution.

Thanks to this unique education of psychological safety, the Muslims were able to overcome the most difficult field turns with reassured hearts and alert minds, to inaugurate a new era in which the Ummah leads the world with the scale of consultation and absolute divine justice.

4. Jurisprudence of Specialization and Integration of Roles in the Muslim Ranks (4. فقه التخصص وتكامل الأدوار في الصف المسلم)

First: Division of Labor and Specializations as a Law for Civilizational Rise (أولاً: تقسيم العمل وتوزيع التخصصات كقانون للنهوض الحضاري)

Building stable societies and achieving field victory and civilizational empowerment cannot be based on cognitive chaos or randomness of opinion, but rather depends primarily on an authentic law from the traditions of Allah in the universe and societies; which is "Division of Labor and Distribution of Specializations" (تقسيم العمل وتوزيع التخصصات). Man alone is an entity incapable of encompassing the various fields of life, and the integration of society requires that each individual fills a gap of the Ummah's gaps commensurate with his individual qualifications, capabilities, and experimental experiences.

In the Islamic conception, specialization does not represent just a modern administrative mechanism, but rather a "legitimate duty" that stems from the core of the texts of revelation that respect human experience and call for entrusting matters to their people. The incident of Al-Hubab bin al-Mundhir singling out the consultation of waters in Badr presents a unique applied model for the "jurisprudence of experts' specialization and the silence of the unqualified"; where the giants of the Companions (like Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali) remained silent out of respect for Al-Hubab's field specialization, while Al-Hubab stepped forward to give his opinion based on his geographical and military experience, which drew for the Muslims a complete military tactic that contributed to deciding the battle.

Second: Legitimate and Quranic Foundation of the Value of Specialization (ثانياً: التأصيل الشرعي والقرآني لقيمة التخصص والخبرة)

The Holy Quran and the noble Prophetic Sunnah laid the foundation for the value of scientific and field specialization, and made referring to the expert a fundamental pillar in making decisions and solving crises; this can be deduced through the following evidence:

  • Asking the people of remembrance and specialization: Allah the Almighty said: {فَاسْأَلُوا أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ إِن كُنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ} ("So ask the people of the message if you do not know.") [Surah An-Nahl: 43] (النحل: 43). Although the original context of the verse relates to asking the people of previous scriptures, the established fundamental rule is: "Consideration is given to the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the reason"; and by virtue of this generality, the verse establishes the reference of the people of specialization in every art and science; so the doctor is asked in medicine, the engineer in engineering, and the military expert in the affairs of war and the field.
  • Reference of those who deduce and owners of the affair: Allah the Almighty said: {وَإِذَا جَاءَهُمْ أَمْرٌ مِّنَ الْأَمْنِ أَوِ الْخَوْفِ أَذَاعُوا بِهِ ۖ وَلَوْ رَدُّوهُ إِلَى الرَّسُولِ وَإِلَىٰ أُولِي الْأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ لَعَلِمَهُ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَنبِطُونَهُ مِنْهُمْ...} ("And when there comes to them information about [public] security or fear, they spread it around. But if they had referred it back to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, then the ones who can derive it from them would have known it.") [Surah An-Nisa: 83] (النساء: 83). The noble verse condemns the chaos of rumors and improvisation in managing security and military crises, and obligates referring dangerous matters to the people of specialization and deduction (experts, analysts, and leaders) who possess the scientific ability to deconstruct events and extract correct estimates.
  • News based on deep knowledge: Allah the Almighty said: {وَلَا يُنَبِّئُكَ مِثْلُ خَبِيرٍ} ("And nothing can inform you like [the One who is] Acquainted.") [Surah Fatir: 14] (فاطر: 14). The verse decides an existential truth; which is that the news issued from deep experimental knowledge and scientific investigation (the expert) exceeds in its value and credibility any other random or improvised news.

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, laid a complete constitution for classifying competencies and valuing specializations within the Muslim society; where he used to clearly announce the points of specialized strength among his companions to direct the Ummah to benefit from them each in its field. Among that is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, in the authentic hadith:

«The most merciful of my Ummah towards my Ummah is Abu Bakr (أبو بكر), the most severe of them in the command of Allah is Umar (عمر), the most truthful of them in modesty is Uthman (عثمان), the most read of them for the Book of Allah is Ubayy bin Ka'b (أُبيّ بن كعب), the most knowledgeable of them in obligations is Zayd bin Thabit (زيد بن ثابت), and the most knowledgeable of them in halal and haram is Mu'adh bin Jabal (معاذ بن جبل)...» [Narrated by At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah].

This hadith represents the first document of "job description and professional classification" in Islam; where the Prophet determined the feature of every science and experience, so the Muslims know to whom they refer when reading the Quran (Ubayy), to whom they refer in dividing inheritances (Zayd), and whom they ask about jurisprudence, halal and haram (Mu'adh).

Third: Deconstructing the Scene of "Silence of the Giants" (ثالثاً: تفكيك مشهد "صمت العمالقة" احتراماً للتخصص)

During the discussion of the camp of Badr and the location of the water wells, the scene included the great Emigrants and Helpers; led by Abu Bakr as-Siddiq with his opinion and sound judgment, Umar bin al-Khattab with his solidity and strategic vision, and Ali bin Abi Talib with his courage and jurisprudence. Despite these giants, none of them stepped forward to propose an amendment to the location of the camp; and the reason for that was not a lack in their intelligence, but rather "the etiquette of specialization and the silence of awe".

The Companions realized that the issue of water wells, the nature of the soil, and the tactics of cutting off water from the enemy was a technical experimental matter that needed a field expert with the paths of the desert and the geography of Badr. As long as none of them possessed this precise experience, they adhered to complete silence to make way for Al-Hubab bin al-Mundhir, who was nicknamed in ignorance and Islam "Dhu al-Ra'y" (ذو الرأي) for his intense knowledge of the arts of war and the terrains of the land.

This collective silence represents the peak of organizational consciousness; as it prevents confusing leadership decisions with general improvised opinions that are not based on a scientific or experimental basis, and makes the final word for the people of experience and the field.

Fourth: Plagues of "Improvisation and Random Opinions" in Crisis Management (رابعاً: آفات "الارتجال والفهلوة" في إدارة الأزمات)

The absence of the jurisprudence of specialization in any society or institution reveals dangerous repercussions that lead to collapse, especially in times of crises and wars: When a climate prevails that allows every individual to talk about everything, "cognitive parasitism" emerges; where the non-specialist talks in medicine, the non-jurist in Sharia, and the non-military in the strategies of war. This transgression leads to marginalizing the real experts, and the rise of showy random opinions that flatter emotions without providing real scientific solutions.

The noble Prophetic Sunnah warned of the danger of losing the scientific trust and entrusting matters to those unqualified; in the authentic hadith narrated by Imam Al-Bukhari, a man asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: When is the Hour? He said: «When the trust is wasted, then wait for the Hour», he said: How is it wasted? He said: «When the matter is entrusted to its non-people, then wait for the Hour.» In another narration by Ibn Majah and Ahmad, he warned of deceptive years in which the "Ruwaybidah" emerges, so they asked him: What is the Ruwaybidah? He said: «The insignificant man who speaks about the affair of the public.»

The emergence of non-specialists to the public affair and management of major crises is an announcement of the ruin of systems, the loss of the prestige of nations, and their field failure; for improvisation cannot stand in the face of the scientific planning of opponents.

Fifth: Symphony of Integration of Roles in the Muslim Ranks (خامساً: سيمفونية تكامل الأدوار في الصف الإسلامي)

Respecting specialization in Badr did not mean marginalizing the rest of the Companions or isolating them, but rather it meant "integration of roles" (Synergy); where everyone worked as one body, in which each member performed his vital function in integration with the rest of the members:

  • Al-Hubab bin al-Mundhir (Logistical and Geographical Specialization): He took charge of drawing the map of waters, wells, and water fortification for the camp.
  • Sa'd bin Mu'adh (Security and Leadership Specialization): He took charge of protecting the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and securing the leadership camp (the Arish [العريش]) and speaking on behalf of the block of Helpers.
  • Mus'ab bin Umayr (Media and Symbolic Specialization): He carried the flag of the greater army, for what he possessed of symbolism and positive influence in the ranks.
  • Az-Zubayr bin al-Awwam and Ali bin Abi Talib (Intelligence and Field Specialization): They led the advanced reconnaissance detachments and guarded the field.
  • The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him (Supreme Leadership and Spiritual Connection): He managed the strategic room of the battle and took charge of supplication, entreaty, and general guidance.

This wonderful symphony of integration of roles and distribution of tasks based on competence and specialization produced an extraordinary combat and organizational energy that enabled a small category (314 fighters) to defeat an army that exceeded it by three times, to decide forever that the Battle of Badr is that victory and civilizational rise are a scientific industry that depends on respecting specialization and integrating roles under the umbrella of rational leadership.

5. Tactic of Securing Leadership and Building Strategic Headquarters: Sa'd bin Mu'adh's Consultation to Build the Arish (5. تكتيك تأمين القيادة وبناء المقر الاستراتيجي: استشارة سعد بن معاذ لبناء العريش)

First: The Principle of "Securing the Center of Gravity" (أولاً: مبدأ "تأمين مركز الثقل" وحماية القيادة العليا)

In contemporary military sciences and national security theories, the concept of "Center of Gravity" (مركز الثقل) represents the fundamental pivot around which the strength of the state or army revolves; and with its collapse or loss, the entire system disintegrates and the morale of the followers collapses. War strategies agree that the "Supreme Leadership" (القيادة العليا) is the most important pillar of this center of gravity; therefore, protecting it, securing it, and providing safe lines of retreat for it in case of a sudden military breakdown is a tactical duty that exceeds in importance winning a round here or there in the battlefield.

In the circumstances of the Great Battle of Badr, the nascent Islamic state in Medina was living through a critical stage of existential establishment; where the survival of the political, call, and legislative entity was linked to the existence of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, alive leading the course. From here, the military and political genius of the Naqib of the Helpers and the master of the Aws, Sa'd bin Mu'adh (سعد بن معاذ), may Allah be pleased with him, was manifested in presenting a complete strategic vision to establish a distinct leadership headquarters and retreated from the ranks, known historically as the "Arish" (العريش). This proposal did not stem from a desire to neutralize the leadership from danger, but rather a conscious reading of the requirements of the continuity of the state and the protection of its national security from complete collapse in case of a field catastrophe.

Second: Details of the Historical Proposal and Its Structural Analysis (ثانياً: تفاصيل المقترح التاريخي لسعد بن معاذ وتحليله البنيوي)

Dependable historical narrations in the Prophetic biography (as in Ibn Hisham and others) mention that Sa'd bin Mu'adh stepped forward to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, before the start of the battle with a complete security and strategic vision, where he said:

"O Prophet of Allah, shall we not build an Arish (العريش) for you to be in, and prepare your mounts with you, then we meet our enemy. If Allah honors us and makes us victorious over our enemy, that is what we love. But if it is the other (defeat), I will sit on your mounts and join those behind us of our people. There are people who stayed behind you, O Prophet of Allah, who are not more intense in their love for you than us. If they had thought you would face war, they would not have stayed behind you. Allah will protect you with them, and they will advise you and strive with you."

This short historical text involves several extremely precise strategic and moral pillars:

  • Sa'd proposed building the "Arish" (which is a shaded canopy of palm fronds) on a high dune overlooking the entire battlefield. This geographical height gives the leadership the ability to monitor the movement of forces, evaluate the paths of the battle, and manage the fighting with full awareness of the field movements of both sides, instead of immersing in the narrow combat details that occupy the leader from managing the overall scene.
  • Sa'd stipulated preparing and equipping the mounts (fast, strong camels) at the leadership headquarters and making them in a state of complete and continuous readiness throughout the battle. This logistical procedure ensures the leadership the ability to withdraw immediately and quickly in case the first defensive lines collapse, overcoming any slowness that may be caused by searching for means of transport in moments of military chaos.
  • Sa'd bin Mu'adh realized with his political consciousness that Medina represented the "strategic depth" for the state, and that the defeat of the army in Badr did not mean the end of the war as long as the supreme leadership was safe and capable of returning to the rear base (Medina); where there was a huge human block and defensive force that did not go out to Badr due to not knowing about the occurrence of war. This force is capable of immediately falling under the banner of the leadership and reorganizing the ranks to repel any future aggression on Medina.
  • The greatness of Sa'd's humanity was manifested in his investment of this difficult situation to defend the Companions who remained in Medina and explain their excuse to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in front of the army: "There are people who stayed behind you, O Prophet of Allah, who are not more intense in their love for you than us..." This reflects Sa'd's keenness on the unity of the rank, and preventing the infiltration of any negative feelings or internal discord between those who witnessed Badr and those who stayed behind in Medina due to not knowing the nature of the exit.

Third: Legitimate Foundation: Combining Infallibility and Exerting Material Causes (ثالثاً: التأصيل العقدي: الجمع بين العصمة وبذل الأسباب المادية)

A cognitive and doctrinal question might come to some minds: How did the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, accept the proposal to build the Arish and secure the mounts for retreat, while he was an infallible Prophet supported by revelation, and promised victory from Allah the Almighty in His saying:

{يَا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ بَلِّغْ مَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ ۖ وَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلْ فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُ ۚ وَاللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النَّاسِ...}
"O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people..." [Surah Al-Ma'idah: 67] (المائدة: 67).

The answer to this lies in the jurisprudence of "combining absolute reliance and exerting material causes"; for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, educates the Ummah with his actions to be a model capable of human emulation after the cessation of revelation.

  • The promise of Allah with infallibility and victory does not cancel the running cosmic laws, nor does it justify for Muslims to neglect security and military measures; rather, the Muslim leader must take the strongest material causes as if they are everything, then rely on Allah as if the causes are nothing.
  • Practicing planning to secure the leadership and tactical retreat when necessary is an application of the traditions of Allah in the earth; and overriding them under the pretext of relying on miracles and divine decree is a blameworthy laziness that contradicts the authentic Islamic methodology.

Fourth: Field Details for Managing the "Arish" Camp (رابعاً: التفاصيل الميدانية لإدارة مقر "العريش")

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, praised Sa'd bin Mu'adh and prayed for good for him, and the proposal was implemented and the Arish was built on the high hill. The guard was organized and the headquarters managed according to the highest standards of discipline and military security:

  1. Elite Guard (Leadership Guard) (حرس القيادة): A battalion of the elite youth of the Helpers, led by Sa'd bin Mu'adh himself, may Allah be pleased with him, took charge of protecting the Arish headquarters; where they stood with their swords drawn at the door of the Arish throughout the battle to prevent any breach or infiltration from the Quraysh cavalry towards the supreme leadership.
  2. The Private Logistical and Security Advisor (المستشار الأمني الخاص): None of the Companions entered the Arish with the Prophet except Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him; to be a direct companion, advisor, and personal guard for him in times of supplication and prayer, which reflects the distinction of Abu Bakr and his special status that manifested previously in the historical journey of the Hijrah and repeated here in the military field.
  3. The Spiritual and Field Operations Room (غرفة العمليات الروحية والميدانية): The Arish turned throughout the battle into an operations room to manage the battle spiritually and in the field; while the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was reviewing the soldiers and distributing tasks, he would enter the Arish to gather spiritual strength with supplication, entreaty, and pleading to Allah the Almighty, drawing the causes of unseen victory that descends to support the earthly causes exerted by the Muslims in the field.

Fifth: The Greatness of Sa'd bin Mu'adh in the Conscience of the Ummah (خامساً: عظمة سعد بن معاذ ومكانته في وجدان الأمة)

This genius position in Badr reveals the early strategic maturity of Sa'd bin Mu'adh, who was looking at events with the eye of a statesman keen on the survival and empowerment of the entire project, not with the eye of an individual fighter enthusiastic for dueling only. This deep wisdom, and the absolute loyalty and dedication that Sa'd showed in various places, explains to us the exceptional status he enjoyed in the noble Prophetic Sunnah; where Imam Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said at his death:

«The Throne of the Most Merciful shook for the death of Sa'd bin Mu'adh (سعد بن معاذ).»

The shaking of the Throne for the death of this young leader (whose Islam did not last for about six years) is a divine announcement of the greatness of this personality who left his immortal mark in the history of Islam; thanks to his great strategic and educational positions that established the security of the state and protected its victorious course in its various critical and fateful stages.

6. Field Miracle and Determining the Death Places of Tyrants by Locations and Names (6. المعجزة الغيبية الميدانية وتحديد مصارع الطغاة بالأسماء والأماكن)

First: Signs of Prophethood and the Educational Function of Unseen Revelation (أولاً: دلائل النبوة والوظيفة التربوية للغيب)

The signs of Prophethood and its material and unseen miracles represent a fundamental pillar for stabilizing faith and manufacturing absolute certainty in the hearts of followers; especially in moments of strategic transformation and the critical historical turns they face with extremely harsh material circumstances. Unseen revelation does not descend just to dazzle minds, but rather performs a delicate educational and psychological function; which is summarized in transferring souls from the realm of "instinctive human fear" of the unknown and death, to the space of "complete spiritual reassurance" of the inevitable divine decree.

In the critical hours that preceded the clash of the ranks in the Great Battle of Badr, the unseen intertwined with the witnessed in a unique field miraculous scene; where the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, walked in the empty battlefield, determining with his noble hand the place of the fall of every tyrant of the masters of Quraysh by name and exact place a full night before the start of the battle. This open and prior material determination reformulated the psychology of the Muslim army, transforming the expected arena of death into a destiny board drawn in detail, and confirming that victory is not a military probability, but an existential truth decreed by the Lord of the Worlds.

Second: Details of the Field Scene on the Night of the Battle (ثانياً: تفاصيل المشهد الميداني ليلة المعركة)
