The purified Prophetic Sunnah documented the details of this unseen miracle with extreme precision and intertwined authentic narrations; among the most authentic is what Imam Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Anas bin Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from Umar bin al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said:

"The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was showing us the death places of the people of Badr yesterday, saying: 'This is the death place of so-and-so tomorrow, if Allah wills', and he placed his hand on the ground: 'This is the death place of so-and-so tomorrow, if Allah wills', and he placed his hand on the ground. Umar bin al-Khattab said: 'None of them swerved (fell behind or moved) from the place of the hand of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him'."

This miraculous Prophetic text reveals delicate features of field certainty:

  • Tangible Material Determination (Placing the hand): The Prophet did not suffice with the general saying that the masters will die, but rather walked in the battlefield and placed his noble palm on the dust in specific places, indicating that the corpse of Utbah bin Rabi'ah will be here, and the corpse of Abu Jahl here, and the corpse of Umayyah bin Khalaf here.
  • Absolute Matching of Reality (None of them swerved): Umar bin al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, swore with the certainty of an eyewitness after the end of the battle, that the bodies of the dead of Quraysh were found exactly matching the places where the Prophet placed his hand on them; not a single corpse deviated from the place of the noble indication even by a handspan, despite the fierceness of the fighting and the random movement of attack and retreat that usually characterizes battles.

Third: Doctrinal Foundation of Prophetic Knowledge of the Unseen (ثالثاً: التأصيل العقدي لعلم الغيب والتعليق بالمشيئة)

This precise unseen prediction involves extremely important doctrinal and legislative dimensions: Among the established origins in the Islamic creed is that absolute knowledge of the unseen is a privilege that Allah the Almighty has kept to Himself; as He, the Majestic and Exalted, said:

{قُل لَّا يَعْلَمُ مَن فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الْغَيْبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ...}
"Say, 'None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except Allah'..." [Surah An-Naml: 65] (النمل: 65).

However, Allah the Almighty may inform His messengers and prophets of parts of this unseen to support their message and show their truthfulness; as He the Almighty said:

{عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ فَلَا يُظْهِرُ عَلَىٰ غَيْبِهِ أَحَدًا * إِلَّا مَنِ ارْتَضَىٰ مِن رَّسُولٍ...}
"[He is] Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His [knowledge of the] unseen to anyone. Except whom He has approved of the messengers..." [Surah Al-Jinn: 26-27] (الجن: 26-27).

Determining the death places of the people of Badr by names and places is of the kind of this miraculous divine informing with which Allah supported His Messenger and the believers in that critical moment.

Despite the Prophet's absolute certainty in the revelation he received, he adhered to the noble Quranic etiquette and restricted his prophecy with the exception by the will of Allah the Blessed and Exalted in every place he pointed to: «This is the death place of so-and-so tomorrow, if Allah wills»; in compliance with the decisive divine command in Surah Al-Kahf:

{وَلَا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إِنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذَٰلِكَ غَدًا * إِلَّا أَن يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ...}
"And never say of anything, 'Indeed, I will do that tomorrow.' Except [when adding], 'If Allah wills'..." [Surah Al-Kahf: 23-24] (الكهف: 23-24).

This commitment to the Quranic etiquette teaches the Ummah that absolute efficacy in the universe is for the will of Allah the Almighty, and linking events to the will is the title of pure servitude and neediness to Allah in every movement and stillness.

Fourth: Educational and Psychological Impact on the Souls of the Companions (رابعاً: الأثر التربوي والنفسي في نفوس الصحابة)

This prior material determination of the death places of the tyrants caused a comprehensive psychological transformation in the souls of the Companions; where it led them to ranks of certainty that exceed ordinary material thinking:

  • Transition from "Knowledge of Certainty" to "Eye of Certainty": The Companions used to believe in the victory of Allah as "knowledge of certainty" based on general Quranic promises. When they saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, placing his hand on the ground and naming the dead of tomorrow with their names and places, they moved to the rank of "eye of certainty"; where they began to see victory manifested before their eyes in the field before the battle started.
  • Crushing the fear of death and dispelling the prestige of the enemy morally: When the Muslim soldier realizes that the leaders of the enemy, their masters, and the owner of the greatest arrogance (Abu Jahl) have had their material end written in specific places under their feet, then the prestige of this enemy vanishes morally completely. The battle turns in the mind of the soldier from a "gamble of unknown consequences" to a "sacred mission to implement the stable destiny decree of last night".

Fifth: The Concluding Scene: Addressing the Lifeless Bodies in the Qalib of Badr (خامساً: المشهد الختامي: خطاب الجثث الهامدة في قليب بدر)

The chapters of this field miracle were completed after the end of the historical battle; where the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered the bodies of the twenty-seven dead of the polytheists (masters of Quraysh and the dead of Badr) to be dragged and thrown into a dry well of the wells of Badr known as the "Qalib" (القليب).

Three days after the end of the battle, according to the authentic narrations in Al-Bukhari and Muslim, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, stood on the edge of the Qalib (القليب), and called these dead by their names and the names of their fathers one by one in a majestic scene that embodies the complete humiliation of tyranny and the absolute victory of truth:

«O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, would it please you that you had obeyed Allah and His Messenger? For we have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?»

Umar bin al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, wondered at this address directed to bodies that had decayed and lost life, so he asked inquiringly: "O Messenger of Allah, what are you addressing to bodies that have no souls?"

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, answered him with a doctrinal answer that decides the truth of the hearing of the dead in that exceptional place, to insist on establishing the argument and the moral humiliation for them: «By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, you do not hear what I say more than them, but they cannot answer.»

Addressing the lifeless bodies in the Qalib (القليب) is the inevitable and logical end of the prophecy that began last night by placing the palm on the dust; for the miraculous picture to be completed, confirming to the Ummah in every time and place that tyranny—no matter how high its pride—then its inevitable fate is falling into the "Qalib" of humiliation and defeat under the weight of certainty and faithful belief committed to divine revelation.

7. Subtleties and Cosmic Measures on the Night of the March: Rain, Drowsiness, and Tranquility (7. اللطائف والتدابير الكونية ليلة الزحف: فقه المطر والنعاس والسكينة)

First: The Cosmic Theater of the Night of the Seventeenth of Ramadan (أولاً: المسرح الكوني ليلة السابع عشر من رمضان)

The Great Battle of Badr was not just a military clash governed by dry material calculations, but rather a theater in which divine destinies interacted with cosmic traditions to manufacture a victory that exceeds the limits of human expectation. On the night of Friday, the seventeenth of the month of Ramadan in the second year of the Hijrah, hearts reached the throats; the numerical and material distance between the two categories was vast, psychological tension cast its shadows on faces, and the field unknown raised natural anxiety in souls.

In that historical night, divine care intervened to prepare the camp of the Muslims through "subtleties and cosmic measures" of extreme precision, spiritual and material gentleness. These measures were not just angelic, but rather represented in the exceptional employment of the basic elements of nature (water and sleep). Rain and drowsiness turned in that night into therapeutic, psychological, and field tools, which steadied the feet of the believers and tied their hearts, and at the same time paralyzed the movement of the enemy and confused their logistical calculations in the same time and place.

Second: The Psychology of "Drowsiness" on the Night of the Battle (ثانياً: سيكولوجية "النعاس" ليلة المعركة)

From a physiological and psychological perspective, quiet sleep on the night of a fateful battle is almost impossible; for fear, anticipation, and responsibility raise the levels of stress hormones (cortisol and adrenaline) in the blood, which causes severe insomnia and nervous and mental tension. This insomnia in turn leads to physical exhaustion and cognitive paralysis that reduces the efficiency of the fighter at the actual clash.

But the divine destinies on the night of Badr canceled this biological law and manufactured a great psychological exception; where Allah descended upon the camp of the Muslims "drowsiness" to cover them all with a quiet, deep sleep. The Holy Quran recorded this exceptional event as a great grace in Surah Al-Anfal:

{إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ النُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةً مِّنْهُ وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيْكُم مَّنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً لِّتُطَهِّرَكُم بِهِ وَيُذْهِبَ عَنكُمْ رِجْزَ الشَّيْطَانِ وَلِيَرْبِطَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِكُمْ وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ الْأَقْدَامَ}
"[Remember] when He overwhelmed you with drowsiness [giving] security from Him and sent down to you from the sky, rain by which to purify you and remove from you the evil [suggestions] of Satan and to make steadfast your hearts and plant firmly thereby the feet." [Surah Al-Anfal: 11] (الأنفال: 11).

This grace was also repeated in Uhud: {ثُمَّ أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّن بَعْدِ الْغَمِّ أَمَنَةً نُّعَاسًا يَغْشَىٰ طَائِفَةً مِّنكُمْ...} ("Then He sent down upon you security after grief, drowsiness overwhelming a faction of you...") [Surah Ali 'Imran: 154] (آل عمران: 154).

The noble Companion Abdullah bin Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, laid a psychological and doctrinal rule in distinguishing between the ranks of drowsiness, where he said: "Drowsiness in fighting is security from Allah, and in prayer it is from Satan" (Narrated by Al-Bukhari in commentary).

Drowsiness during fear is evidence of "tranquility" (السكينة); because the soul surrendered to the decree of Allah is reassured and its anxiety subsides, so its nervous system relaxes and surrenders to sleep. The Companions expressed the depth of this drowsiness on the night of Badr with precise phrases:

  • Az-Zubayr bin al-Awwam, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Drowsiness overcame us that night, until I would tighten myself (to keep from sleeping), then the ground would throw me down (I would fall on it), and I could not do but that."
  • Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I saw myself with my chin in front of me, and I do not feel until I fall on my side."
  • Rifa'ah bin Rafi', may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Drowsiness struck the Muslims that night, it was cast upon them so they slept."

This divine drowsiness worked as a "reset button" for the nervous and physical system of the Muslims. While the polytheists spent their night in tension, anxiety, dancing, and artificial singing to hide their internal fear, the Muslims slept a quiet sleep. They woke up in the morning with full physical activity, clear alert minds, and hearts filled with confidence and calm, which gave them an enormous moral advantage at the start of the battle.

Third: The Cosmic Paradox of Rain (ثالثاً: المفارقة الكونية للمطر)

The grace of drowsiness coincided with a second grace no less precise and gentle; which is the descent of rain in that night. The rain was not ordinary, but rather a sign in detailing its physical and psychological impact between the two adjacent camps; where it descended as a mercy and steadying for the believers, and descended as an obstacle and disturbance for the polytheists.

The Muslims camped in a part of the valley of Badr characterized by its fine, loose sandy soil (called in the tongue of the Arabs "dahas sand"); which is a soil that is difficult to walk or run on, and the feet of men and the hooves of horses sink in it. Above this geographical crisis, the polytheists had taken control of the main water wells, so the Muslims were left without enough water for drinking or purification.

Here Satan exploited this loophole and began to spread his toxic whispers in the souls of some Companions (the evil of Satan): "You claim that you are the allies of Allah and His Messenger is among you, yet the polytheists have overcome you to the water, and you pray with dust while in a state of major impurity, performing tayammum on the sands in which your feet sink? How will you be victorious?"

The rains descended on the night of Badr as a light, gentle drizzle, to perform three strategic functions mentioned by the Quran with precision in Surah Al-Anfal:

  • Sensory and Moral Purification ({لِّتُطَهِّرَكُم بِهِ}): Those in a state of major impurity bathed, and the thirsty performed ablution, and water was provided for drinking, which removed the physiological need.
  • Crushing Satanic Doubts ({وَيُذْهِبَ عَنكُمْ رِجْزَ الشَّيْطَانِ}): The whispers of Satan vanished completely with the descent of water and purification, and the souls regained their certainty in Allah's care for them.
  • Geological and Field Steadying ({وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ الْأَقْدَامَ}): The fine, loose sand turned by the light rain into a cohesive, hard soil (compaction of the earth). This compaction enabled the feet and the hooves of horses to run, stand, attack and retreat without sinking or slipping, so Allah tied their hearts sensibly and meaningfully.

In the same night and with the same clouds, the rain poured on the camp of the polytheists in a completely different manner; where it descended as a severe, flooding torrent that flooded their land. Because the nature of the land they camped in was thick clay, the severe rain turned into sticky mud and slippery clay. This mud paralyzed the movement of their horses and camels, made the movement of their infantry difficult, caused hindrance to their logistical advance, and spread in their souls a feeling of catastrophe and disturbance before the fight.

This physical and field contrast of a single natural element (water) that descended on two adjacent camps represents the peak of divine management and the cosmic paradox that confirms the direct care of Allah for the ranks of the believers.

Fourth: Servitude and Prophetic Wakefulness on the Night of the March (رابعاً: مقام العبودية واليقظة النبوية ليلة الزحف)

While the entire army of Muslims slept under the weight of quiet faithful drowsiness and spiritual tranquility, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, penned a unique model in the wakefulness of the leader, his humbling, and his servitude to Allah the Almighty.

Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad with an authentic chain of narration from the hadith of Ali bin Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: «There was no rider among us on the day of Badr except Al-Miqdad, and I saw us with no one among us sleeping except the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, under a tree, praying and weeping until morning.»

In another narration by An-Nasa'i: «He was praying to a tree and supplicating until morning.»

This Prophetic wakefulness reveals the highest station of servitude for the leader; for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not sleep that night for the following considerations:

  • Supplication and Seeking Victory: He knew the greatness of the responsibility and the fatefulness of the meeting; so he spent the night conversing with his Lord with words that make hearts tremble, spreading his noble hands until his cloak fell from his shoulders, saying: «O Allah, if You destroy this group today, You will not be worshipped on earth after today...»
  • Guarding and Field Arrangement: He was supervising the securing of the camp with the vanguard of the guard (like Abu Qatadah al-Harith bin Rib'i, whom the Prophet prayed for protection because he guarded him that night).
  • Prayer with Tears of Longing and Neediness: He was weeping in humbling to his Lord until dawn.

When dawn broke, he called out with the voice of the leader certain of victory: «Prayer, O servants of Allah», so the Companions came with activity from under the trees and shields they had taken shelter from the rain with, so he led them in the morning prayer, and urged them to fight with unyielding determination.

The cosmic subtleties on the night of Badr (drowsiness, rain, and Prophetic wakefulness) certainly prove that victory and empowerment require the combination of earthly causes with divine support; while the soldiers slept to restore their physical and psychological strength with drowsiness and rain, the leader stayed awake to connect the earth with the sky with prayer and entreaty, so the army deserved to have tranquility and angels descend upon it in the morning to write the greatest lines of glory in the history of Islam.

8. Philosophy of Single Combat in Ancient Wars and Its Psychological Impact (8. فلسفة المبارزة الفردية في الحروب القديمة وأثرها النفسي)

First: The Psychology of Dueling as a Tool to Decide the Battle of Wills (أولاً: سيكولوجية المبارزة كأداة لحسم صراع الإرادات)

Single combat (The Duel) in ancient wars was not just an enthusiastic tradition or a display of physical strength and combat skills, but rather an extremely important military and psychological tool subject to the laws of the clash of wills. In the absence of modern means of communication, the battle was decided morally before it started materially; for the psychology of the masses dictates that the fate of the heroes and symbols, negatively or positively, is reflected on the morale of the entire army.

The opening duel in ancient wars represents three strategic functions:

  1. War of Nerves and Psychological Probing: Where the two armies stand in complete silence, their sights are focused on a small spot where the options narrow between death and life; whoever controls this area controls the morale of the entire battle.
  2. Shock of Symbols and Breaking Moral Leadership: The killing of the first-class hero in an army does not represent just a numerical loss (one in a thousand), but rather a fatal blow to the symbolism of strength and arrogant superiority in the souls of the ordinary soldiers.
  3. Moral Charging and Inaugurating the Doctrine of Fighting: The victory of the hero of the weak category gives it an extraordinary psychological momentum, charges the souls with courage and boldness, and removes any remaining awe from the material superiority of the enemy.

In the Great Battle of Badr, the scene of the single duel was the actual gateway to opening the battle; where the tribal pride of Quraysh intertwined with the courage, responsibility, and absolute loyalty to the family of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Helpers, to end the scene with a terrible shock that shattered the morale of Quraysh and broke the back of their pride before the start of the general clash.

Second: Details of the Field Scene of the Historical Duel of Badr (ثانياً: تفاصيل المشهد الميداني للمبارزة التاريخية في بدر)

Dependable historical narrations in the biographies and Sahihs (as in Sahih Al-Bukhari and Sunan Abi Dawud) mention that with the beginning of the clash of the ranks and the approach of the two armies, three heavy knights emerged from the camp of the polytheists, representing the military and political elite of Mecca:

  • Utbah bin Rabi'ah (عتبة بن ربيعة): One of the masters of Quraysh, its great sages, and its leaders.
  • Shaybah bin Rabi'ah (شيبة بن ربيعة): The brother of Utbah and one of the counted knights of Mecca.
  • Al-Walid bin Utbah (الوليد بن عتبة): The son of Utbah, a fierce young hero of the heroes of Quraysh.

These three stood between the two ranks shouting with insolence and ignorant pride: "Who will duel?" Immediately, three young men from the Helpers of the people of Medina rushed to go out for the duel, and they are:

  • Awf bin al-Harith (عوف بن الحارث), may Allah be pleased with him.
  • Mu'awwidh bin al-Harith (معوذ بن الحارث), may Allah be pleased with him.
  • Abdullah bin Rawahah (عبد الله بن رواحة), may Allah be pleased with him.

When they stood in front of the knights of Mecca, Utbah asked them with caution and the complacency of the Qurashi who rises above fighting the unqualified in the standards of ignorance: "Who are you?", they said: "A group of the Helpers." Utbah said with insolent tribal pride: "Noble peers, we have no need for you, we only want our cousins." Then their caller called out in a loud voice heard by the camp of the Muslims: "O Muhammad, bring out to us our peers from our people (i.e., from Quraysh)."

In this critical moment, the greatness of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the unique rules of military justice were manifested; for he did not send from the general people or those recently converted to Islam to test the courage of the knights of Mecca in them, but rather he presented his sons, relatives, and closest kin to be in the first line of death and confrontation; and this is the peak of altruism and field example.

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, called out saying with a decisive voice: «Rise, O Ubaydah bin al-Harith (عبيدة بن الحارث), and rise, O Hamzah (حمزة), and rise, O Ali (علي).»

The three, may Allah be pleased with them, rose like mountains, brandishing their swords. When they approached the knights of Mecca, Utbah asked them: "Who are you?", they said: "Ubaydah, Hamzah, and Ali." Utbah said with satisfaction and acceptance: "Yes, noble peers."

  • The First Round (Al-Walid bin Utbah against Ali bin Abi Talib): The youngest of the two categories met; Ali bin Abi Talib (who was a young youth in the prime of his youth) with the fierce Al-Walid bin Utbah. The round lasted only a few seconds; as Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, attacked like a thunderbolt and rushed Al-Walid with a decisive sword strike that cut off his head and killed him immediately.
  • The Second Round (Shaybah bin Rabi'ah against Hamzah bin Abdul-Muttalib): The champion knight Hamzah bin Abdul-Muttalib (Lion of Allah and His Messenger) met Shaybah bin Rabi'ah. With the same speed and decisiveness, Hamzah, may Allah be pleased with him, closed in on Shaybah and rushed him with a cutting sword strike that joined him with his nephew Al-Walid dead on the spot.
  • The Third and Fiercest Round (Utbah bin Rabi'ah against Ubaydah bin al-Harith): The oldest of the two categories met; Ubaydah bin al-Harith (who was an old sheikh approaching sixty or seventy) with Utbah bin Rabi'ah. This round was the fiercest and longest; as two courageous strikes differed between them, Ubaydah hit Utbah and injured him, and Utbah hit Ubaydah on his leg and cut it (or inflicted a severe deep wound on it), and the two fell covered in blood.
  • Deciding the Scene and the Lightning End: Ali and Hamzah, may Allah be pleased with them, did not stand with their hands tied; rather, they immediately attacked with their swords on Utbah bin Rabi'ah and finished him off, and carried their cousin Ubaydah bin al-Harith while his leg was bleeding abundantly, and returned with him to the camp of the Muslims amidst the takbeers of victory and the overwhelming joy that shook the desert.

When they carried Ubaydah, may Allah be pleased with him, and placed him in front of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, he pulled his noble face and placed the bloody foot of Ubaydah in his lap to soothe him. Ubaydah looked with the eye of the faithful believer sincere to the Messenger of Allah and asked him with the eagerness of a lover longing for divine acceptance: "Am I a martyr, O Messenger of Allah?"

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, answered him with a flood of mercy and certainty: «Yes, you are a martyr.»

Ubaydah, may Allah be pleased with him, said with the consciousness of the Companion affected by loyalty and responsibility: "If Abu Talib were alive, he would know that he has told the truth when he said: (And we will surrender him until we are prostrated around him, and we are distracted from our children and wives)." Ubaydah died after the battle by a few days affected by his wounds on the way back in the area of "As-Safra'" (الصفراء) and was buried there, to be the first martyr from the family of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in the great battles.

Third: Doctrinal and Quranic Foundation of the Duel (ثالثاً: التأصيل العقدي والقرآني للمبارزة)

This great historical incident did not pass as a fleeting military event, but rather the Holy Quran descended to record it in the tablets of revelation as a pivotal doctrinal issue that distinguishes between two methodologies and two disputants; where Imam Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him, that he used to swear a righteous oath: "That this verse: {These are two adversaries who have disagreed over [the matter of] their Lord...} was revealed about these six on the day of Badr: Hamzah, Ali, Ubaydah bin al-Harith, Utbah, Shaybah, and Al-Walid bin Utbah" [Sahih Al-Bukhari: 3965].

The Quranic text came decisively to state the fate of the two factions:

{۞ هَٰذَانِ خَصْمَانِ اخْتَصَمُوا فِي رَبِّهِمْ ۖ فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيَابٌ مِّن نَّارٍ يُصَبُّ مِن فَوْقِ رُءُوسِهِمُ الْحَمِيمُ * يُصْهَرُ بِهِ مَا فِي بُطُونِهِمْ وَالْجُلُودُ * وَلَهُم مَّقَامِعُ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ}
"These are two adversaries who have disagreed over [the matter of] their Lord. But those who disbelieved - garments of fire will be cut out for them. Poured upon their heads from within will be scalding water. By which is melted that within their bellies and [their] skins. And for them are hooked rods of iron." [Surah Al-Hajj: 19-21] (الحج: 19-21).

This Quranic foundation teaches the Ummah that the battle in its core is not a battle over spoils, influence, or dust, but rather a decisive doctrinal battle between truth and falsehood, and between monotheism and polytheism; therefore, this field dispute deserved lines in the Book of Allah recited until the Day of Judgment to immortalize the certainty established in the hearts of the Companions.

Fourth: Psychological and Strategic Impact of the Duel on the Two Camps (رابعاً: الأثر النفسي والاستراتيجي للمبارزة على المعسكرين)

The single duel in Badr achieved enormous strategic and psychological results that changed the course of the actual fighting:

  • The Terrible Psychological Shock for the Camp of Quraysh: Utbah and Shaybah were the pillars of the army and its decision-makers, and Al-Walid represented the youth and young strength of Quraysh. The killing of these three together and in a few minutes with lightning strikes formed a terrible shock that overthrew the moral spirit of Quraysh completely; as the soldiers suddenly felt that their strength and pride had collapsed in a few minutes before the swords of the Muslims, so panic crept into their ranks and they began to blame each other and doubt the usefulness of fighting.
  • The Enormous Moral Charge for the Camp of Muslims: The Muslims saw with their own eyes how the masters of disbelief were struck down with lightning strikes by their brothers, so any remaining awe of the material or numerical superiority of the enemy vanished from their souls; and they became certain that victory was near and that their swords were capable of deciding the battle, so their hearts were filled with boldness, love of meeting, and looking forward to completing the victory.
  • The Leadership Example of the Family of the House: The duel established the culture of "leadership by example" in the souls of the Muslims; for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would not sacrifice the sons of others, but rather he presented his family first, which increased the loyalty of the Companions and their absolute confidence in their just, courageous leadership that advances in the places of death and prefers others with life and safety.

Thanks to this lightning opening round, the Muslims entered the battle with reassured, desperate hearts, while the polytheists entered it with trembling, morally defeated hearts; for the Battle of Badr to prove forever that breaking the pride of the enemy and deciding the battle of wills represents half the victory before the start of the actual fighting in the field.

9. Psychology of Those Hastening to Paradise: The Story of Umayr bin al-Humam and Throwing the Dates (9. سيكولوجية المسارعين إلى الجنة: قصة عمير بن الحمام وإلقاء التمرات)

First: Reformulating Time and the Concept of "Long Life" (أولاً: إعادة صياغة الزمن ومفهوم "الحياة الطويلة")

"Faith motivation" is one of the deepest psychological phenomena studied by behavioral and educational sciences; for firm belief has the ability to completely reformulate the human cognitive system, and change its basic concepts towards issues of existence, death, time, and utility. In contemporary psychology, how a person deals with time represents an indicator of the nature of his priorities and goals; for time lengthens in a person's feeling or shortens according to the extent of his longing for the goal he is waiting for.

On the morning of the Great Battle of Badr, the field recorded an extraordinary behavioral model for this psychological philosophy; embodied by the noble Companion Umayr bin al-Humam al-Ansari (عمير بن الحمام الأنصاري), may Allah be pleased with him. With decisive Prophetic words, and an infallible promise of Paradise, an immediate and sudden shift occurred in his scale of priorities, until merely waiting a few minutes to eat a few dates represented in his view a "long life" that he could not bear the patience of remaining in, thus overcoming the instinct of hunger and the love of survival, to inaugurate the school of "those hastening to Paradise" who saw the unseen with the eye of certainty, and shortened the distance of time with a sword strike.

Second: Details of the Historical Incident (Narration of Sahih Muslim) (ثانياً: تفاصيل الواقعة في صحيح مسلم)

The purified Prophetic Sunnah documented this exceptional historical event with the highest degrees of authenticity and methodological documentation; where Imam Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Anas bin Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, in the context of the events of the Battle of Badr:

«The polytheists approached, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Rise to a Paradise whose width is as the width of the heavens and the earth.' Umayr bin al-Humam al-Ansari said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Bakh, Bakh!' The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'What makes you say Bakh, Bakh?' He said: 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, only the hope that I will be among its people.' He said: 'Then you are among its people.' He took out dates from his quiver, and began to eat from them, then said: 'If I live until I eat these dates of mine, it would be a long life!' He threw what he had of dates, then fought them until he was killed.» [Sahih Muslim: 1901].

This Prophetic text reveals a unique psychological and worship path:

  • The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, launched the call to war with the phrase: «Rise to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth»; and this direction represents a smart linking of the field to the Hereafter. He did not say to them "Rise to spoils" or "Rise to fight Quraysh"; rather, he immediately transferred their minds to what is beyond nature.
  • The conscience of Umayr bin al-Humam was shaken by this huge geographical picture of Paradise, so he inquired, clarifying and astonished: "A Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth?", the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, confirmed the truth for him: «Yes.»
  • Umayr launched his spontaneous phrase: "Bakh, Bakh!"; which is a word that the Arabs used to say to magnify the matter, aggrandize the status, and show overwhelming joy, absolute satisfaction, and beautiful astonishment at the greatness of the good news.
  • When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, asked him about his motive for saying it: «What makes you say Bakh, Bakh?», Umayr expressed with honesty and dedication his only wish: "Hope that I will be among its people"; then came the infallible Prophetic certificate that falsehood does not come to it from before it or behind it: «Then you are among its people.»

This word was not just a supplication, but rather an "infallible testimony" of Paradise that the ear of Umayr received, so the unseen turned in his second into a tangible material reality; for Paradise became waiting for him directly behind the limits of this perishing body.

Third: Quranic Foundation of Presenting Paradise and Hastening to It (ثالثاً: التأصيل القرآني لتقديم الجنة والمسارعة إليها)

The Prophetic call in Badr is linked to Muhkamat verses that formulated the mental and spiritual conception of the Companions towards the reality of Paradise and the inevitability of hastening and racing to it:

  • Faith Hastening: Allah the Almighty said: {وَسَارِعُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ} ("And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden as wide as the heavens and earth, prepared for the righteous.") [Surah Ali 'Imran: 133] (آل عمران: 133).
  • Destiny Racing: Allah the Almighty said: {سَابِقُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا كَعَرْضِ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ أُعِدَّتْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ...} ("Race to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden whose width is like the width of the heavens and earth, prepared for those who believed in Allah and His messengers...") [Surah Al-Hadid: 21] (الحديد: 21).

These verses implanted in the souls of the first generation the culture of "initiative and rapid escape"; for Paradise is not attained by sitting, wishing, and procrastination, but by racing, hastening, diligent work, and striving with souls and wealth.

Fourth: Psychological Analysis of Umayr's Phrase: "It would be a long life!" (رابعاً: التحليل النفسي لعبارة عمير: "إنها لحياة طويلة!")

The phrase of Umayr bin al-Humam: "If I live until I eat these dates of mine, it would be a long life!" represents rich material for behavioral and educational analysis; as it reveals several exceptional psychological features:

Dates in the desert represented the material of survival, the food of the fighter, and the favorite sweet of the soldier; and it is a material that satisfies a physiological instinctive need (hunger and the energy of the body). In that critical moment, Umayr looked at the dates in his noble palm, so a sudden real asceticism occurred in him towards this material; as he saw that being occupied with the mechanism of material survival (eating food for three minutes) represented a disruption of his supreme purpose, which was embracing eternity in Paradise.

The memory of the biography here invokes the great Quranic scene of the Prophet of Allah Musa, peace be upon him, when he hastened to meet his Lord at the Tur, leaving his people behind; his Lord asked him: {وَمَا أَعْجَلَكَ عَن قَوْمِكَ يَا مُوسَىٰ} ("And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses?"), he answered with the tongue of a lover longing: {قَالَ هُمْ أُولَاءِ عَلَىٰ أَثَرِي وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَىٰ} ("He said, 'They are close upon my tracks, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You be pleased'.") [Surah Taha: 83-84] (طه: 83-84).

Umayr bin al-Humam applied the same methodology; so he hastened to leave his food, his soul, and his life, and threw the dates to be the state of his article and his saying: "And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You be pleased and meet"; for the meeting with Allah was his only goal that did not accept delay for even a few seconds.

Fifth: The Philosophy of "Selling the Soul" and the Integration of Behavior (خامساً: فلسفة "بيع النفس" وتكامل السلوك مع اليقين)

Throwing the dates and rushing towards the swords of the polytheists was not suicide or despair of life, but rather a practical application of the great Quranic deal in which the believer sells his soul to his Lord willingly and out of love; as Allah the Almighty said:

{۞ إِنَّ اللَّهَ اشْتَرَىٰ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُم بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ ۚ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَيَقْتُلُونَ وَيُقْتَلُونَ ۖ وَعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا فِي التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنجِيلِ وَالْقُرْآنِ...}
"Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties [in exchange] for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise [binding] upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Quran..." [Surah At-Tawbah: 111] (التوبة: 111).

This exceptional psychological behavior was repeated among the great Companions in various places; in the Battle of Uhud, the scene was repeated with Anas bin an-Nadr (أنس بن النضر), may Allah be pleased with him (the uncle of Anas bin Malik); when the people were shaken and the killing of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was rumored, and some Companions saw that they had thrown down their weapons, he said to them: "What are you doing with life after him? Rise and die upon what he died upon", then he rushed and said to Sa'd bin Mu'adh: "O Sa'd, by the fragrance of Paradise! I find its fragrance from behind Uhud", so he fought until eighty-something sword strikes and spear thrusts were found in him.

The Ummah whose heroes and soldiers see that their remaining a few minutes to eat dates represents an obstacle and a long life, and find the fragrance of Paradise blowing on them from behind the mountains, is an Ummah whose soldiers possess an overwhelming psychological strength and self-immunity against the fear of death. This sublime faith motivation becomes the moral weapon that shatters the pride of any military opponent, and writes with its blood and sacrifices the chapters of eternal glory and sovereignty in the records of history.

10. Response of Destiny to the Supplication of Those Seeking Judgment (10. استجابة القدر لدعاء المستفتحين: "إن تستفتحوا فقد جاءكم الفتح")

First: The Psychology of Arrogance and the Trap of Destined Judgment (أولاً: سيكولوجية الغطرسة ومصيدة الاستفتاح القدري)

In the philosophy of divine traditions governing the universe, arrogance and pride represent a thick veil that blinds the insight of tyrants from seeing objective truths; for the psychology of "self-deception" among them reaches a rank that makes them believe with certainty that the sky stands on their side, and that destinies are employed to protect their influence and pride. From here, the autocrat falls into the worst strategic and psychological mistake a human can commit; which is calling upon Allah the Blessed and Exalted and descending His decisive destined judgment (Istiftah / الاستفتاح), thinking that he possesses the papers of piety and virtue, so his supplication turns into a weapon that destroys his kingdom and eradicates his root.

Istiftah (الاستفتاح) in the tongue of the Arabs revolves around two intertwined meanings:

  • The First: Seeking victory and help.
  • The Second: Seeking judgment and ruling between the two adversaries. The Mustaftih (المستفتح) is the one who asks the judge or destiny to decide the dispute, show the truthful, and destroy the falsifier.

On the day of the Great Battle of Badr, these two implications gathered in a strange tragic position; when the Pharaoh of this Ummah, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, stood with all his pride and arrogance, raising his hands with entreaty, seeking judgment and descending the decisive judgment of Allah, and specifying with his tongue the standards of destruction, so the destinies responded to his supplication to the letter, but upon him and his party; for the Battle of Badr to decide forever that the traditions of Allah do not favor anyone, and the supplication of the wrongdoer against himself is the gateway through which destiny shortens the time of his inevitable end.

Second: Details of the Historical Incident: The Supplication of Abu Jahl Before the Battle (ثانياً: تفاصيل الواقعة: دعاء أبي جهل قبل المعركة)

The texts of the Prophetic biography and interpretive traditions (as proven in Sunan An-Nasa'i Al-Kubra, Mustadrak Al-Hakim, and the interpretations of At-Tabari and Ibn Kathir) converged in narrating the details of the Istiftah (الاستفتاح) supplication that Abu Jahl bin Hisham pleaded with on the night of the battle or just before the clash directly.

After the two crowds became visible, Abu Jahl bin Hisham stood raising his hands to the sky, seeking help from Allah, seeking judgment against the Muslims, and using the finest terms of values and morals to defend falsehood; where he said:

"O Allah, whoever among us severs the ties of kinship and brings what is not known, destroy him in the morning (i.e., destroy and humiliate him this morning)."

In another authentic narration narrated by Imam Ahmad and An-Nasa'i from the hadith of Abdullah bin Tha'labah bin Su'ayr, may Allah be pleased with him:

"O Allah, whoever among us severs the ties of kinship and brings what is not known, destroy him in the morning."

In a third narration from the biographies: "O Allah, whoever among us is most beloved to You and most pleasing to You, support him today."

This supplication reveals amazing levels of mental falsification and inverted consciousness:

  1. Trying the Truth with the Scale of the Familiar Family: Abu Jahl bin Hisham saw with certainty that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was the one who severed the ties of kinship; because he parted from his religion, separated the son from his father, and made social discord within the houses of Mecca. He saw that Islam was "what was not known" because it contradicted the heritage of the fathers and grandfathers and the worship of idols; so he asked for Istiftah based on this distorted apparent perspective.
  2. Absence of Awareness of the Reality of Faith-Based Severing of Ties: It was absent from the dark consciousness of Abu Jahl bin Hisham that Quraysh was the one who truly severed the ties of kinship; when they tortured their sons, expelled them from their homes without right except that they say 'Our Lord is Allah', confiscated their money, and cut off the bonds of kinship and ties under the pretexts of polytheism and pride.
  3. Blind Confidence in Material Victory: The numerical abundance and the luxurious military equipment of Quraysh drove Abu Jahl bin Hisham to believe that Allah must support him; for the prevailing in the scales of matter is the owner of the multitude, so this arrogance led him to venture to ask for "direct destined judgment".

Third: Quranic Foundation of Istiftah (Deconstructing Surah Al-Anfal, Verse 19) (ثالثاً: التأصيل القرآني للاستفتاح: تفكيك الآية 19 من سورة الأنفال)

The Holy Quran did not leave this position to pass without a decisive legislative and doctrinal comment; rather, the verses descended immediately after the end of the battle to address the disbelievers of Quraysh and reveal to them how their overwhelming defeat and the killing of their leaders was the direct and complete divine response to the supplication of Abu Jahl bin Hisham. Allah the Blessed and Exalted said in Surah Al-Anfal:

{إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُوا فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الْفَتْحُ ۖ وَإِن تَنتَهُوا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ ۖ وَإِن تَعُودُوا نَعُدْ وَلَن تُغْنِيَ عَنكُمْ فِئَتُكُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَوْ كَثُرَتْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ}
"If you [disbelievers] seek a judgment - the judgment has come to you; and if you desist - it is better for you. But if you return [to sin], We will return. And never will you benefit from your company anything, even if it increased. And that is because Allah is the ally of the believers." [Surah Al-Anfal: 19] (الأنفال: 19).

  • If you seek judgment ({إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُوا}): Meaning, if you have asked—O people of Quraysh on the tongue of Abu Jahl—for the separation, judgment, and ruling between you and Muhammad, and the distinction between the truthful and the falsifier, the oppressor and the committed to the truth.
  • The judgment has come to you ({فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الْفَتْحُ}): The "Fath" (الفتح) here is the "historical judgment and separation". Allah has responded to you to the letter; so He destroyed your severer of ties (who was Abu Jahl bin Hisham and the masters of Mecca), and supported the truthful, oppressed category that adhered to the faith-based ties and brought pure monotheism.
  • Destined Sarcasm and Strict Punishment: The verse represents a kind of "divine reprimand and sarcasm" of the tyrants; for you are the ones who hastened your end by asking for judgment, and Allah has judged between you and placed the corpses of your Mustaftih and leaders in the Qalib of Badr blamed and driven away.

Fourth: Evidence of Interpretation and Hadith on the Reason for Revelation (رابعاً: شواهد التفسير والحديث في سبب النزول)

The imams of interpretation and tradition agreed on the connection of this noble verse to the supplication of Abu Jahl; among these evidences:

  • Narration of As-Suddi (السدي): He said in the interpretation of the verse: "The polytheists, when they left Mecca to Badr, took hold of the curtains of the Kaaba, sought victory from Allah, and said: 'O Allah, support the highest of the two armies, the most generous of the two categories, and the most virtuous of the two tribes.' When they arrived in Badr, Abu Jahl said: 'O Allah, whoever among us severs the ties of kinship... so Allah descended: {If you seek a judgment - the judgment has come to you}'."
  • Narration of Ibn Abbas (ابن عباس), may Allah be pleased with them both: He said: "Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: 'O Allah, whoever among us severs the ties of kinship and brings what is not known, destroy him in the morning.' That was an Istiftah from him, so Allah descended this verse" (Narrated by Al-Hakim in Al-Mustadrak and authenticated).

Fifth: Psychological and Educational Lessons of the "Law of Destined Istiftah" (خامساً: الدروس النفسية والتربوية لقانون الاستفتاح القدري)

This strange scene in Badr presents a package of deep psychological and educational lessons that run as a past tradition in the lives of nations and individuals:

  1. The Tradition of Gradual Luring with False Obedience: The tyrant may reach a rank of blindness that makes him practice obedience, worship, and supplication as a tool to pass his oppression; so he calls upon Allah with the truth as a falsification, without feeling that he is driving himself to his doom. This teaches us that the lesson is not in the beauty of the wording and the formula of the supplication, but in the reality of the heart and the dedication of the behavior from oppression and aggression.
  2. The Reversal of the Psychological Weapon on Its Owner: Abu Jahl wanted with his supplication to charge the morale of his army and establish in their souls that they were the "people of truth", the guards of the temple and the old traditions. But the overwhelming defeat and his killing specifically made this supplication psychologically reverse on Quraysh as the strongest evidence of their misguidance; as the sages of Mecca later realized that the supplication of Abu Jahl had actually been answered, and that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, was the truthful one brought near to Allah, which paved the way for many of them to enter Islam after that due to this intellectual and emotional shock.
  3. The Day of Criterion and Clarification of Truths: The polytheists wanted the Fath (judgment), so the decisive divine Fath came, which Allah named its day as the "Day of Criterion" (يوم الفرقان); as He the Almighty said: {...يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ...} ("...on the day of criterion, the day the two armies met...") [Surah Al-Anfal: 41] (الأنفال: 41). This day was a true criterion that clarified to the worlds who is the reformer and who is the corrupter, for destinies to remain holding the reins of initiative, answering the supplications of the sincere Mustaftihs, and breaking the backs of the tyrannical Mustaftihs with their ignorance and arrogance.

11. Intertwining of Material Causes and Unseen Support: The Pebble Throw and Battles of Angels (11. تشابك الأسباب المادية والمدد الغيبي: رمية الحصى ومعارك الملائكة)

First: The Creed of the Intertwining of Earthly Traditions and Heavenly Support (أولاً: عقيدة التشابك بين السنن الأرضية والمدد السماوي)

The Islamic conception of the traditions of victory and empowerment presents a unique model that combines harmoniously and integrally between the world of witness (matter and causes) and the world of the unseen (support and divine aid). Islam completely rejects the sheer material deviation that idolizes earthly causes and cancels divine laws, just as it rejects the lazy deviation that disables material work waiting for wonders and miracles. The governing law for the victory of Allah is summarized in: "Exerting the maximum possible human material effort (the station of exerting the cause), then the divine unseen support and aid descends (the station of reliance and support) crowning and completing the human effort, not a substitute for it."

In the Great Battle of Badr, this miraculous intertwining and clash between cause and support was manifested in its clearest forms; where the descent of the angels and the Prophetic pebble throw were not to disable the swords of the Companions or discourage their determination, but rather the support descended as a crown that crowns their blood, sacrifices, and complete material effort, for the battle to decide an eternal rule: that true victory is not the product of matter alone, but rather good news and steadying from the Almighty, the Wise, for whoever exerted his utmost effort on earth seeking help from the sky.

Second: The Physical Genius of the Prophetic Throw (ثانياً: العبقرية الفيزيائية للرمية النبوية)

At the peak of the field clash and the escalation of the fierceness of the fighting, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, resorted to activating a simple material cause in its appearance, miraculous in its core and cosmic impact; where he took a handful of dust and small pebbles, faced the faces of the army of Quraysh with them, and threw them while shouting in a voice that shook their morale: «Shahat al-wujuh» (i.e., may the faces of disbelief be disgraced and uglified).

The material-unseen miracle happened; for that handful did not leave an eye, a nostril, or a mouth of any of the polytheists (the thousand fighters) except that it filled it with dust and pebbles, so they were occupied with the dust in their eyes, panic and temporary blindness crept into them, their power was broken, and they retreated defeated.

The Holy Quran recorded this miraculous intertwining between the human act and the divine impact in Surah Al-Anfal with a phrase overflowing with eloquence and doctrinal depth:

{فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ ۚ وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمَىٰ ۚ وَلِيُبْلِيَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْهُ بَلَاءً حَسَنًا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ}
"And you did not kill them, but Allah killed them. And you threw not, [O Muhammad], when you threw, but Allah threw. And [He did so] that He may test the believers with a good test. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing." [Surah Al-Anfal: 17] (الأنفال: 17).

The noble verse divides the throwing process into three cognitive levels:

  1. The First Negation ({فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ ... وَمَا رَمَيْتَ}): Negation of the final impact resulting from the throw; for it is not within the power of a human in the usual physical laws to throw a handful of dust with his hand to reach and hit the eyes of a thousand fighters in a vast area; so this extraordinary impact is negated from the human capability of the Messenger.
  2. The Second Affirmation ({إِذْ رَمَيْتَ}): Affirmation of the material act and the sensory human effort; for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, took the dust, grasped it with his noble hand, and exerted the muscular force in directing it and throwing it towards the enemy, and this is the "station of exerting the cause" required from the servant.
  3. The Third Decisive Attribution ({وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمَىٰ}): Attribution of the delivery, communication, and true efficacy of the impact to the Causer of causes, the Almighty; for Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, is the One who carried the atoms of the dust to enter the eyes of a thousand fighters at once, so the simple material throw turned into a weapon that disabled the enemy's ability to fight.

Third: Battles of Angels and the Supporting Unseen Aid (ثالثاً: معارك الملائكة والمدد الغيبي المظاهر)

The unseen support in Badr was not limited to the Prophetic throw, but the noble angels descended by the command of their Lord to support the camp of the Muslims and steady their feet. The Holy Quran documented this descent in several places:

  • The First Support with (One Thousand) Angels: Allah the Almighty said: {إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ فَاسْتَجَابَ لَكُمْ أَنِّي مُمِدُّكُم بِأَلْفٍ مِّنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ} ("[Remember] when you asked help of your Lord, and He answered you, 'I will reinforce you with a thousand from the angels, following one another'.") [Surah Al-Anfal: 9] (الأنفال: 9).
  • Support with (Three Thousand) and (Five Thousand) upon Patience and Piety: Allah the Almighty said in Surah Ali 'Imran: {إِذْ تَقُولُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَلَن يَكْفِيَكُمْ أَن يُمِدَّكُمْ رَبُّكُم بِثَلَاثَةِ آلَافٍ مِّنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُنزَلِينَ * بَلَىٰ ۚ إِن تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا وَيَأْتُوكُم مِّن فَوْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا يُمْدِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُم بِخَمْسَةِ آلَافٍ مِّنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُسَوِّمِينَ} ("[Remember] when you said to the believers, 'Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?' Yes, if you remain patient and conscious of Allah and they come [attacking] you in rage, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels having marks [of distinction].") [Surah Ali 'Imran: 124-125] (آل عمران: 124-125).

The Quran specified the nature of the work of the angels in Badr clearly; as their tasks were divided between moral support for the believers, and sensory and material punishment of the disbelievers:

{إِذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ إِلَى الْمَلَائِكَةِ أَنِّي مَعَكُمْ فَثَبِّتُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ۚ سَأُلْقِي فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الرُّعْبَ فَاضْرِبُوا فَوْقَ الْأَعْنَاقِ وَاضْرِبُوا مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنَانٍ}
"[Remember] when your Lord inspired to the angels, 'I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast into the hearts of those who disbelieved terror, so strike [them] upon the necks and strike from them every fingertip'." [Surah Al-Anfal: 12] (الأنفال: 12).

  • The Task of Faith and Moral Steadying ({فَثَبِّتُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا}): The angels were appearing and whispering in the hearts of the believers with good news and security, and appearing before them to increase their certainty in the support and victory.
  • The Task of Moral Terrifying of the Disbelievers ({سَأُلْقِي فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الرُّعْبَ}): Allah cast terror into the hearts of the polytheists just by hearing and seeing strange movements and deafening sounds in the field.
  • The Task of Sensory and Direct Fighting ({فَاضْرِبُوا فَوْقَ الْأَعْنَاقِ}): The angels participated in killing and striking with hands, swords, and whips, and their strikes had distinct marks that the Companions distinguished.

The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, recorded strange field phenomena that prove the sensory presence of the angels in Badr; among these evidences:

  • The Voice of the Whip and the Caller (Aqdim Hayzum): Imam Muslim narrated in his Sahih from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "While a man of the Muslims on that day was running after a man of the polytheists in front of him, he heard a strike with a whip above him, and the voice of the rider saying: 'Aqdim Hayzum!' (Advance, Hayzum!). He looked at the polytheist in front of him and he fell on his back. He looked at him and found his nose cut off, and his face split like the strike of a whip, so it all turned green. The Ansari came and told the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, so he said: 'You told the truth, that is from the support of the third heaven'." [Sahih Muslim: 1763]. (Hayzum is the name of the angel's horse).
  • Heads Flying Before the Swords Reach: From Abu Dawud al-Mazini, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I was following a man of the polytheists to strike him, when his head fell before my sword reached him, so I knew that someone else had killed him."
  • The Miracle of the Capture of Abbas bin Abdul-Muttalib (عباس بن عبد المطلب): The short, weak Ansari Abu al-Yusr (Ka'b bin Amr), may Allah be pleased with him, stepped forward carrying Abbas bin Abdul-Muttalib (the uncle of the Prophet, who was huge and strong) as a prisoner. When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saw them, he wondered at how Abu al-Yusr was able to capture Abbas, so Abbas said, correcting with the consciousness of a witness: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, this one did not capture me; rather, I was captured by a bald man, of the most handsome people in face, on a piebald horse, and I do not see him among the people!" The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Abu al-Yusr with a smile: «Be silent, for Allah the Almighty has supported you with a noble angel» [Narrated by Ahmad and Al-Hakim and authenticated].

Fourth: The Strategic Wisdom of Seeking Help from Angels Instead of Direct Annihilation (رابعاً: الحكمة الاستراتيجية من استنزال الملائكة دون الإهلاك المباشر)

Here a deep cognitive question emerges: Why did Allah send angels fighting with swords and whips, while He the Almighty is capable with a single angel (like Jibreel, peace be upon him, with a strike from his wing) to eradicate the army of Quraysh and everyone on the earth in the blink of an eye?

The answer lies in the jurisprudence of "Educational Building and Human Responsibility":

  1. The Inevitability of Exerting Human Effort for the Vicegerency of the Earth: Allah the Blessed and Exalted does not lead the battles of the believers with silent miracles and the complete annihilation of opponents without human effort; because this cancels the value of trial, jihad, sacrifice, and practical education of the Ummah. The Ummah that suffices with waiting for the heavenly annihilation of enemies is a lazy Ummah that does not deserve the development of the earth nor the sovereignty over it.
  2. Angels as Good News and Steadying, Not as a Substitute for the Sword: The Holy Quran decided this strategic cause with complete clarity in Surah Al-Anfal:

    {وَمَا جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشْرَىٰ وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ بِهِ قُلُوبُكُمْ ۚ وَمَا النَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ}
    "And Allah did not make it except as good news and to reassure your hearts thereby. And victory is not but from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise." [Surah Al-Anfal: 10] (الأنفال: 10).

    The angels did not descend for the Companions to sleep and they fight on their behalf; rather, they descended to reassure the hearts and give good news to the minds with the support, while the physical effort, piercing with spears, striking with swords, and bleeding with blood remains the field duty required from the Companions to complete the deal with Allah the Almighty.

The intertwining of material causes and unseen support in Badr (the pebble throw and the battles of angels) remains the supreme lesson for the callers, the mujahideen, and the reformers in every era: that your duty is to prepare what is possible of sensory and organizational strength on the earth with all honesty and vigilance, and when your material power reaches its end and your minds and hearts are sincere in reliance; the curtains of the unseen will open for you, and the divine support will descend carrying the atoms of the dust to enter the eyes of the opponents, and employing the soldiers of the sky to lead the Ummah towards the horizons of eternal victory and empowerment.

Element 1: Heroics of the Senior Companions in the Epic of Badr (العنصر الأول: بطولات الصحابة الكبار في ملحمة بدر)

The Great Battle of Badr (غزوة بدر الكبرى) constituted the first real test in which the true mettle of men emerged and extraordinary leadership models were established in Islamic history. The battle was not merely a military confrontation between two groups; rather, it was an arena in which the loftiest manifestations of steadfastness, sacrifice, and absolute devotion were displayed. On this day, the senior Companions (الصحابة) — may Allah be pleased with them — authored an exceptional epic of valor and loyalty, making their combat behavior a fundamental and educational benchmark for combining physical strength with spiritual certainty.

1. Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam (الزبير بن العوام) (The Disciple of the Messenger) .. The Steadfastness of Wounds and the Honor of the Sword

The noble Companion Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam (الزبير بن العوام) — may Allah be pleased with him — stood out on the day of Badr as one of the greatest knights of the field and among the most valiant. He wore a yellow headband that distinguished him in combat, and it was reported in historical narrations that the angels descended on that day wearing the same mark as Al-Zubayr (الزبير) and riding horses resembling his.

Al-Zubayr (الزبير) fought the battle with fierce bravery and bold assault, sustaining deep and severe wounds in his body. It was recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (صحيح البخاري) on the authority of his son 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr (عروة بن الزبير) that he said:

"Al-Zubayr had three sword wounds: one of them was on his shoulder into which I could insert my fingers; two were inflicted on the day of Badr, and one on the day of Yarmouk."

These wounds demonstrate the depth of striking power and the ferocity of close-quarters combat that Al-Zubayr (الزبير) engaged in; his shoulder was split by a deep strike, the mark of which remained a visible trace where his child could insert his fingers. His bravery was not limited to bearing severe wounds; it was also manifested in the force of his blow, which impacted his weapon itself. The intensity of his strike caused a "Fullah" (فُلّة — a notch or crack in the blade of the sword). His descendants kept this historic sword as a glorious relic, so much so that when the Caliph 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan (عبد الملك بن مروان) later saw the sword of Al-Zubayr (الزبير), he quoted the verse of Al-Nabighah al-Dhubyani (النابغة الذبياني): "In them are notches from clashing with enemy battalions."

Despite these wounds and the fracture in his sword's blade, Al-Zubayr (الزبير) continued fighting without retreat, establishing the concept of "fighting bravely to the very end."

2. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (سعد بن أبي وقاص) .. The Protector of Leadership and the One Whose Supplication Is Answered

Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (سعد بن أبي وقاص) — may Allah be pleased with him — represented the striking power in archery and tactical missile capability on the day of Badr. He was the first person to shoot an arrow in the cause of Allah in Islamic history.

The heroism of Sa'd (سعد) at Badr manifested in two strategic dimensions:

  • Guarding and Covering the Leadership: Sa'd (سعد) appointed himself as a direct guard and defender of the person of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم). He placed his body and honor in front of the supreme leadership, shooting arrows at the polytheists with high density and extreme accuracy to prevent any approach to the position of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم).
  • Unique Prophetic Honor (Invoking Both Parents in Ransom): In recognition of this bravery and accuracy in protecting the rank, Sa'd (سعد) achieved a unique virtue unsurpassed by anyone else. The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) combined both of his parents in a ransom invocation for him. It is established in Al-Sahihayn (الصحيحين) on the authority of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (علي بن أبي طالب) — may Allah be pleased with him — that he said:

    "I never heard the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) combine his parents for anyone other than Sa'd; I heard him say on the day of Badr: 'Shoot, O Sa'd, may my father and mother be ransomed for you!'"

Sa'd's (سعد) shooting was not merely an abstract physical action; he blended it with earnest supplication and faith-driven conviction. He would shoot the arrow while supplicating in his prayer and on the field: "O Allah, shake their feet, and cast terror into their hearts," upon which the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) would respond with his famous prayer: "O Allah, answer Sa'd when he supplicates to You." Thus, his arrows never missed a target, and his prayers descended like thunderbolts upon the morale of his opponents.

3. Mu'adh ibn 'Afra (معاذ بن عفراء) .. Absolute Devotion and the Impulse Toward Martyrdom

The young Companion Mu'adh ibn al-Harith (معاذ بن الحارث) — known as Ibn 'Afra (ابن عفراء), attributed to his mother Al-'Afra bint 'Ubayd (العفراء بنت عبيد) — may Allah be pleased with him, recorded a stance emanating from spirituality and military devotion that transcended material calculations.

Amid the heat of battle and the rising dust of combat, Mu'adh (معاذ) approached the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) asking a question that pierced to the core of the spiritual philosophy of Jihad:

"O Messenger of Allah, what makes the Lord laugh with pleasure at His servant?"

The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) answered him with a word that summarized the concept of absolute heroism:

"His plunging his hand into the enemy unarmored (hasiran — بدون درع)." (Meaning engaging the enemy's ranks without a protective coat of mail or helmet).

As soon as Mu'adh (معاذ) heard these glad tidings, he took off his iron armor that was protecting him from blows and threw it to the ground, stripping himself of every material barrier between him and martyrdom. He drew his sword and plunged his body into the heart of the polytheists' masses, striking them and tearing through their ranks until he fell as a martyr on the land of Badr.

The stance of Ibn 'Afra (ابن عفراء) established an educational principle for the Ummah: that longing for Allah's pleasure and Paradise can, in decisive moments, negate all calculations of material protection, transforming martyrdom into a goal sought for its own sake.

4. Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib (حمزة بن عبد المطلب) (The Lion of Allah) .. The Awe of the Banner and the Terror of the Champions

Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib (حمزة بن عبد المطلب) — may Allah be pleased with him — was the embodiment of awe and combat boldness in the battle. He distinguished himself on the field by placing an "ostrich feather" on his chest, which was a sign of challenge and distinction used by Arab knights to inform their enemies of their location and invite them to duels.

Hamzah (حمزة) created a state of psychological terror in the ranks of Quraish (قريش) on the day of Badr due to his sweeping assault and strikes that harvested the leaders of disbelief and the nobles of Makkah (مكة). The testimony of his enemies to his valor is evident in what was narrated about Umayyah ibn Khalaf (أمية بن خلف) — one of the greatest tyrants of Makkah. When he was captured after the battle, he asked 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Auf (عبد الرحمن بن عوف) about the knight who marked his chest with an ostrich feather. When told, "That was Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib," Umayyah (أمية) said in awe and resignation:

"That is the one who wrought havoc upon us!"

Hamzah (حمزة) did not fight in a cautious, defensive style; rather, he moved through the field like a raging lion, deciding direct encounters and stabilizing the ranks of the Muslims with his presence on the ground, making him a moral symbol of courageous military leadership and embodying the Divine saying:

{يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا لَقِيتُمْ فِئَةً فَاثْبُتُوا وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ}
"O you who have believed, when you encounter a company [from the enemy], stand firm and remember Allah much that you may succeed" [Surah Al-Anfal: 45] (الأنفال: 45).

Element 2: "The Cubs of Badr" and the High Ambition of Youth and Adolescents (Under 18) (العنصر الثاني: "أشبال بدر" وعلو همة الفتيان والشباب)

The Great Battle of Badr (غزوة بدر الكبرى) was not merely a battle between fully grown knights; it was a historic milestone that redefined the concept of "youth" and adolescence in human thought. At a time when pre-Islamic and contemporary systems deal with the stage of youth as a period of reckless whim or irresponsible adolescence, Islam demonstrated its capacity to sharpen the ambitions of the young, converting boys who had not exceeded eighteen years of age into heroes bearing the concerns of the Ummah and driving major strategic transformations. Badr was a living application of the eternal Quranic verse:

{إِنَّهُمْ فِتْيَةٌ آمَنُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ وَزِدْنَاهُمْ هُدًى}
"Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance" [Surah Al-Kahf: 13] (الكهف: 13).

1. The Phenomenon of Competing for Martyrdom and Crying Upon Rejection

The Muslim camp prior to setting out for Badr witnessed a unique phenomenon in military history: intense crowding and pushing among boys and youths to register their names among the combatants. When the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) inspected the army and rejected those under the age of military obligation (which was generally fifteen years in military rulings), the decision of rejection did not fall upon the hearts of these youths as a chance for safety; rather, it landed like a tragedy that unleashed their tears and grief.

Prominent among those turned back due to their young age were:

  • Usamah ibn Zaid ibn Harithah (أسامة بن زيد بن حارثة) (the beloved of the Messenger of Allah).
  • 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب).
  • Zaid ibn Arqam (زيد بن أرقم).
  • Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (البراء بن عازب).
  • Rafi' ibn Khadij (رافع بن خديج).

It is established in Al-Sahihayn (الصحيحين) on the authority of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (عبد الله بن عمر) — may Allah be pleased with them both — that he said:

"The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) inspected me on the day of Badr when I was thirteen years old, and he turned me back."

This deep weeping upon being turned back revealed a completely different value system among these youths, where competition was directed toward sacrifice and offering one's soul, not toward safety and comfort.

2. Zayd ibn Thabit (زيد بن ثابت) .. The Genius of Transforming Rejection into Scientific Achievement

When the young Zayd ibn Thabit al-Ansari (زيد بن ثابت الأنصاري) — may Allah be pleased with him (who was about thirteen years old at the time) — was turned back and not permitted to carry a sword at Badr due to his small stature, he did not surrender to feelings of frustration and despair. Nor did he withdraw to the margins; instead, with educational intelligence and spiritual resolve, he shifted to another frontier no less important than the battlefield: the frontier of scientific and intelligence Jihad.

His mother, Al-Nuwar bint Malik (النوار بنت مالك), brought him to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is our son Zayd ibn Thabit; he memorizes seventeen Surahs of the Book of Allah..." The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) listened to him, was impressed by his intelligence and quick memorization, and assigned him a specialized strategic mission related to state security and diplomacy: learning the language of the Jews (Hebrew/Syriac) to encode correspondence and read the documents of opponents.

Imam Al-Tirmidhi (الترمذي) and Abu Dawud (أبو داود) narrated with an authentic chain on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit (زيد بن ثابت) — may Allah be pleased with him — that he said:

"The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) commanded me, so I learned the writing of the Jews for him. He said: 'By Allah, I do not trust the Jews with my letters.' Not even half a month passed before I mastered it. I would write for him when he wrote, and read to him when letters were written to him."

Zayd (زيد) accomplished the learning of a complete language — reading, writing, and speaking — in only seventeen days, announcing to the world that "the youth who was denied carrying a sword at Badr" had become the founder of the "Signal and Strategic Translation Corps" in the Islamic state, later becoming the compiler of the Holy Quran and one of the greatest scholars of the Ummah in inheritance law and Quranic recitations.

3. 'Umair ibn Abi Waqqas (عمير بن أبي وقاص) .. Complete Passion for Martyrdom and Overcoming Young Age

The young 'Umair ibn Abi Waqqas (عمير بن أبي وقاص) — may Allah be pleased with him (brother of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (سعد بن أبي وقاص), who was approximately sixteen years old at the time) — recorded a scene of the highest longing for martyrdom and hiding out of eagerness to contribute.

His brother, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (سعد بن أبي وقاص) — may Allah be pleased with him — narrates the details of this stance, saying:

"I saw my brother 'Umair ibn Abi Waqqas hiding before the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) inspected us on the day of Badr. I said: 'What is the matter with you, my brother?' He said: 'I fear that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) will see me, consider me too young, and turn me back, while I love to go out so that Allah might grant me martyrdom.'"

When the army was inspected, the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) saw him, considered him too young, and ordered him to return. 'Umair (عمير) wept so intensely and bitterly that it shook the emotions of those present. The Prophet's (صلى الله عليه وسلم) heart softened for him, and he granted him permission to go out. Sa'd (سعد) says: "I used to tie the belt of his sword due to his small size," as the sword was longer than his small stature, so his brother would raise the sword belt and tighten its knot so it would not drag on the ground.

'Umair (عمير) fought at Badr like a hero and was martyred on the battlefield at the hands of 'Amr ibn Wudd al-'Amiri (عمرو بن ود العامري), becoming the first youth martyr in the battle.

4. The Epic of Killing Abu Jahl (أبو جهل) .. When Youths Overthrow the Thrones of Tyranny

Badr witnessed one of the most astonishing combat epics when two young Ansar youths (around fourteen or fifteen years of age) accomplished the elimination of the military and moral authority of the fiercest tyrant on earth: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham (أبو جهل بن هشام).

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari (صحيح البخاري) and Sahih Muslim (صحيح مسلم) on the authority of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Auf (عبد الرحمن بن عوف) — may Allah be pleased with him — that he said:

"While I was standing in the rank on the day of Badr, I looked to my right and left, and behold, I was between two young boys of the Ansar (الأنصار), young in age. I wished I were between stronger men. One of them nudged me and said: 'O uncle, do you know Abu Jahl?' I said: 'Yes, what do you need with him, O son of my brother?' He said: 'I was informed that he curses the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم). By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, if I see him, my shadow will not leave his shadow until the swiftest of us to die dies!' I was amazed by that. Then the other nudged me and said the same to me."

The two boys were Mu'adh ibn 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh (معاذ بن عمرو بن الجموح) and Mu'awwidh ibn 'Afra (معوذ بن عفراء) — may Allah be pleased with them both.

Details of the Field Epic:

  • Penetrating the Forest of Spears: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Auf (عبد الرحمن بن عوف) pointed Abu Jahl (أبو جهل) out to them while he was moving under heavy guard by Quraish (قريش) knights, resembling a dense forest of interwoven spears.
  • The Swoop of Falcons: The two youths swooped down upon Abu Jahl (أبو جهل) like striking falcons, penetrating human barriers and guarding swords.
  • The Swift Leg Strike: Mu'adh ibn 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh (معاذ بن عمرو بن الجموح) dealt him a swift sword strike that severed his leg. Mu'adh (معاذ) said: "I targeted Abu Jahl and struck him a blow that sent his foot and half his leg flying. By Allah, I can only compare it to a date-stone flying from beneath a pestle when struck."
  • The Astounding Heroism of Mu'adh ibn 'Amr (معاذ بن عمرو) (Severing the Dangling Arm): During the fight, 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl (عكرمة بن أبي جهل) attacked Mu'adh (معاذ) and struck his shoulder, leaving his arm hanging by a piece of skin at his side. Mu'adh (معاذ) describes this legendary scene in biography literature (Sirat Ibn Hisham — سيرة ابن هشام), saying:

    "I fought for the rest of my day dragging it behind me. When it bothered me, I placed my foot upon it, then leaned over it until I severed it!" He stepped on his severed arm with his foot and pulled his body upward until he completely detached it from his body so it would not hinder him from continuing to defend the Messenger of Allah!

  • The Finishing Blows by Mu'awwidh (معوذ) and Ibn Mas'ud (ابن مسعود): Mu'awwidh ibn 'Afra (معوذ بن عفراء) followed up on Abu Jahl (أبو جهل) with further strikes until he left him taking his final breaths (Mu'awwidh then fought until he was martyred). At the end of the battle, 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (عبد الله بن مسعود) — may Allah be pleased with him — checked the slain polytheists and found Abu Jahl (أبو جهل) in his death throes. He severed his head and brought it to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), whereupon the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) announced the end of this tyrant's era by saying: "This is the Pharaoh of this Ummah."

5. Harithah ibn Suraqah al-Ansari (حارثة بن سراقة الأنصاري) .. The Stray Arrow and the Tidings of Al-Firdaus Al-A'la

The youth Harithah ibn Suraqah al-Ansari (حارثة بن سراقة الأنصاري) — may Allah be pleased with him — recorded another model of the blessing of martyrdom at Badr. While standing near the rear by the water basin watching the field, he was struck by a "Sahm Gharab" (سهم غَرَب — a stray arrow from an unknown source and shooter) that struck his throat, killing him instantly.

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari (صحيح البخاري) on the authority of Anas ibn Malik (أنس بن مالك) — may Allah be pleased with him — that the mother of Harithah, Al-Rubayyi' bint al-Nadr (الرُبيّع بنت النضر), came to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) after the battle and said:

"O Prophet of Allah, will you not tell me about Harithah? — he was killed on the day of Badr by a stray arrow — If he is in Paradise, I will be patient; if it is otherwise, I shall weep for him intensely!"

The Prophetic response established a new standard for the ranks of the martyrs of Badr:
